He looked good in his first game back, totaling over 200 yards and scoring three touchdowns on the night, including one impressive rushing touchdown from over ten yards out. He and Kansas City's offense as a whole are looking promising right now and may be primed for a big season if they can stay healthy this year.

news.body: Trevor Lawrence completed 17 of his 29 passes for 189 yards and an interception while adding six yards on two rushes in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
news.head: Trevor Lawrence throws for 189 yards in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Lawrence got the Jaguars off to a fast start as they were leading 10-3 at halftime, but the Broncos came to life on defense starting in the third quarter. Lawrence has now thrown for 434 yards and four touchdowns through the first two games of the season. He will be a solid QB1 in fantasy in Week 3 against the Patriots.

news.body: Trevor Lawrence completed 18-of-23 passes for 245 yards and four touchdowns in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns. He also ran twice for three yards.
news.head: Trevor Lawrence flawless in big win over Browns
news.impact: Lawrence played on easy mode against a Browns defense that just couldn't create stops. He had only five incompletions to four touchdowns on the day, a great ratio to have. With their win over the Browns, the Jags are the only AFC South team to clinch a win on Sunday. He faces a much tougher test against the Broncos next week.

news.body: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said he is “trending toward” playing the starters in Friday’s preseason game against the Panthers.
news.head: Trevor Lawrence: Jaguars starters 'trending' towards playing Friday
news.impact: The Jaguars starters did not see the field in last week's preseason opener. If they do play, it'll likely be in limited fashion.

news.body: Trevor Lawrence completed 22-of-30 passes for 255 yards and three touchdowns in the Jaguars 41-7 win over the Titans. He also ran twice for 11 yards.
news.head: Trevor Lawrence tosses three touchdowns in win
news.impact: Lawrence capped off a great season with a dominant performance against the lowly Titans. It wasn't always pretty, and there were plenty of struggles early on this season, but HC Liam Coen and Lawrence were able to get things rolling. The team is looking like they could be a tough out in the postseason, but time will tell.

news.body: Tyler Shough completed 29-of-42 passes for 255 yards with four touchdowns and one interception in the Saints 35-27 loss against the Raiders on Sunday.
news.head: Tyler Shough throws four touchdowns, struggles with turnovers late
news.impact: Shough was dealing through the first three quarters, tossing four touchdowns with two of them going to Juwan Johnson and the other two going to Noah Fant. The Saints turned the ball over four times in the fourth quarter with three of them being committed by Shough on an interception and two fumbles. He'll face the Falcons next week.

news.body: Tyler Shough completed 27-of-34 passes for 252 yards and one touchdown in a 24-17 win over the Ravens.
news.head: Tyler Shough executes late comeback win in Week 2
news.impact: Shough also added 23 rushing yards on nine carries in the win. Both of the second-year quarterback's touchdowns came in the fourth quarter to tie the game and give the Saints the lead. Shough has looked great through his first two games of the season and will look to build on these performances in a Week 3 matchup with Las Vegas.

news.body: Tyler Shough completed 35-of-56 pass attempts for 410 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions while also rushing four times for eight yards in the Saints' 31-30 Week 1 overtime loss to the Detroit Lions.
news.head: Tyler Shough electrifies late in Week 1 loss to Lions
news.impact: Shough carried the New Orleans offense late in the contest after trailing 21-0 at one point, throwing three second-half touchdowns to force overtime in the Week 1 loss. The second-year signal-caller faces a stiff test in Week 2 against a tough Baltimore Ravens defense next.

news.body: Tyler Shough completed 23-of-35 passes for 259 yards with one touchdown and one interception in the Saints 19-17 loss against the Falcons.
news.head: Tyler Shough throws for 259 yards in Week 18
news.impact: Shough added another 34 yards on the ground. The rookie closed the season on a high note with New Orleans. He should remain the starter heading into next season for the Saints.

news.body: Aaron Jones Sr. ran for 58 yards on 17 carries in the Vikings 23-16 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday. He also caught 5-of-6 targets for 34 yards receiving.
news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. totals 22 touches Sunday
news.impact: It wasn't the most efficient performance for Jones, but his overall volume made up for it. He'll be an RB2 play next week against the Dolphins.

news.body: Aaron Jones Sr. is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. (knee) off injury report Sunday
news.impact: Jones was able to return to practice to finish the week. He should remain an RB2 play in a lead role in the Vikings backfield.

news.body: Aaron Jones Sr. practiced again on Friday.
news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. (knee) practices Friday
news.impact: Jones was limited in his return to practice on Thursday. He should be in line for another lead role on Sunday against the Buccaneers. He'll be an RB2 play for fantasy managers.

news.body: Aaron Jones Sr. (knee) returned to Minnesota's practice as a limited participant on Thursday.
news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. (knee) returns to practice Thursday
news.impact: The veteran was unable to practice due to a knee issue on Wednesday, but he returned to practice on Thursday and was able to participate in a limited fashion. He's tracking towards playing in Week 3, but we won't know his official status for Sunday's game until sometime after practice on Friday.

news.body: Alvin Kamara ran for 36 yards on nine carries in the Saints 35-27 loss against the Raiders on Sunday. He also caught his lone target for five yards receiving.
news.head: Alvin Kamara sees nine carries Sunday
news.impact: Kamara saw his role expand after Travis Etienne Jr. left the game early. He'll be in the flex conversation next week if Etienne is sidelined.

news.body: Alvin Kamara rushed for 15 yards on nine carries in the Saints' 24-17 win over the Ravens. He caught 5-of-6 targets for seven yards.
news.head: Alvin Kamara hauls in five passes in Week 2 win
news.impact: Kamara was very limited in his production in his 2026 debut, was clearly a focal point of the offense which cut into Travis Etienne's volume. Fantasy managers will want to be cautious with both running backs volume in question heading into a Week 3 matchup with Las Vegas.

news.body: Alvin Kamara is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
news.head: Alvin Kamara (knee) off injury report for Week 2
news.impact: Kamara will be good to go for his season debut. He should be in a third down/passing down role in the Saints backfield behind Travis Etienne.

news.body: Alvin Kamara (knee) practiced in a full capacity again on Thursday.
news.head: Alvin Kamara (knee) practices in full again Thursday
news.impact: The veteran running back was again a full participant at practice on Thursday, making him very likely to play in Sunday's game against Baltimore. His expected presence will likely take some work away from both Kendre Miller and Travis Etienne Jr. moving forward.

news.body: Ashton Jeanty ran for 56 yards on 19 carries in the Raiders 35-27 win over the Saints. He also caught 3-of-3 targets for 36 yards receiving.
news.head: Ashton Jeanty struggles on ground Sunday
news.impact: Jeanty was inefficient on the ground for the second straight week. He still remained active in the passing game. He remains an RB1 in a workhorse role moving forward.

news.body: Ashton Jeanty rushed the ball 21 times for 48 yards and caught 4-of-7 targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: Ashton Jeanty inefficient in win Sunday
news.impact: Jeanty didn't look great on Sunday. He totaled just 63 on his 28 opportunities against the Chargers, and he wasn't able to get into the end zone at all, which left him with an underwhelming fantasy total. The Raiders have a tough schedule coming up, so the young running back will need to step up his game if he wants to deliver for fantasy managers.

news.body: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) logged a full practice session on Wednesday.
news.head: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) logs full practice Wednesday
news.impact: Jeanty seems to be entirely over his ankle injury at this point, as he played through it in Week 1 and now logs a full practice session to start the week on Wednesday. He should be a full go and high-quality fantasy option moving forward, assuming he suffers no setbacks with his recovery.

news.body: Ashton Jeanty carried the ball 23 times for 102 yards while also hauling in all six of his targets for a team-leading 45 yards and two touchdowns in the Raiders' 27-13 Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Ashton Jeanty leads offense in Week 1 win over Dolphins
news.impact: Jeanty was dynamic out of the backfield in the season opener, leading the team in rushing and receiving yards in the win. the running back remains an elite RB1 option with PPR upside for fantasy managers ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers ahead.

news.body: Bhayshul Tuten carried the ball 13 times for 65 yards and a touchdown while catching both of his targets for minus-three yards in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
news.head: Bhayshul Tuten finds the end zone in Week 2
news.impact: Tuten punched in a one-yard touchdown in the second quarter to give the Jaguars an early 7-0 lead. The second-year back also vastly outproduced Chris Rodriguez Jr., who had just 13 yards on six carries. Tuten has now racked up 131 rushing yards through two games. He will be a solid RB2 in fantasy heading into Week 3 against the Patriots.

news.body: Bhayshul Tuten ran 15 times for 66 yards in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday. He also caught his only target for 22 yards.
news.head: Bhayshul Tuten racks up 66 yards on the ground in win
news.impact: Tuten led the Jags in rushing attempts in the win, but didn't have much to show in terms of fantasy scoring in half- or full-PPR formats. But to be fair, he was efficient in his touches, and it's likely that better days are ahead for the apparent Jags RB1.

news.body: Bhayshul Tuten is expected to “have a big year” according to HC Liam Coen. Coen praised the second year back in an interview, noting his explosive ability and the growth in his game.
news.head: Bhayshul Tuten expected to ‘have a big year’ per HC Coen
news.impact: Tuten is the favorite for RB1 duties in Jacksonville with his do-it-all skillset, while Chris Rodriguez dealing with an injury this offseason and LeQuint Allen is primarily a pass blocking and catching specialist. He’s still a bit of an unknown since Travis Etienne handled the majority of backfield work in 2025, but his upside should things work out is tantalizing.

news.body: Bhayshul Tuten ran five times for 23 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 41-7 win over the Titans on Sunday.
news.head: Bhayshul Tuten gets five touches in return
news.impact: Tuten didn't touch the ball much in his return to play, but it's important to note that he was the RB2 of the offense, putting LeQuint Allen back in his special teams role.

news.body: Bijan Robinson ran 29 times for 194 yards and two touchdowns and caught both of his targets for 19 yards in the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
news.head: Bijan Robinson explodes in Week 3 win over Packers
news.impact: Robinson had his way with the Packers' defense, rushing for 6.7 yards per carry. He ripped off a huge 55-yard gain early on in the game, which opened the floodgates for many more big runs throughout the game. The Packers simply could not stop him, and once the ground game got going, QB Michael Penix and WR Drake London were able to carve up the Packers' secondary. With Penix back, the offense has new life, and Bijan stands to benefit greatly from it, even if Brian Robinson Jr. spells him.

news.body: Bijan Robinson ran 16 times for 72 yards and caught three of four targets for nine yards in the Falcons' 34-3 blowout loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
news.head: Bijan Robinson held in check in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Robinson was fine on the ground, 4.5 yards per carry, but still largely held in check. The Panthers didn't allow the Falcons to move the ball, mostly thanks to Atlanta's lack of competent QB play. If Michael Penix returns on Thursday, that will hopefully be a huge boost to Bijan's value. If not, it's looking like another long night for Bijan managers.

news.body: Bijan Robinson carried the ball 21 times for 83 yards and caught eight of his 10 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in a 20-13 loss to the Steelers in Week 1.
news.head: Bijan Robinson hauls in touchdown catch in Week 1
news.impact: Robinson was basically the entire offense for the Falcons in the close loss to Pittsburgh. He scored the team's only touchdown on a 23-yard catch at the end of the first quarter. It was an excellent start to the season for the star running back, who will slot in as a high-end RB1 in fantasy heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Panthers.

news.body: Bijan Robinson has agreed to a three-year, $75 million contract extension with the Atlanta Falcons according to Adam Schefter.
news.head: Bijan Robinson agrees to three-year extension with Falcons
news.impact: The deal includes $51 million in guaranteed money while also making Robinson the highest-paid running back in the league. The third-year back finished with 2,298 total offensive yards and 11 total touchdowns in 2025 and remains in the argument as the 1.01 pick in upcoming fantasy drafts with offensive minded Kevin Stefanski being named the new head coach this offseason for the Falcons.

news.body: Blake Corum rushed the ball 12 times for 79 yards and caught one pass for 13 yards in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
news.head: Blake Corum totals 92 yards in win Monday
news.impact: Los Angeles' offense looked great on Monday night, and Corum was no exception to that. He put up 92 total yards on just 13 opportunities, although he wasn't able to get into the endzone to put the capstone on that. The Rams' backfield is a situation to continue monitoring, with Corum and Kyren Williams each seeing the same amount of carries in this blowout win.

news.body: Blake Corum ran 10 times for 54 yards in the Rams' 27-7 loss to the 49ers on Thursday.
news.head: Blake Corum totals 54 yards in loss
news.impact: Corum was solid on the ground at 5.4 a carry, but that was about all he had going for him. Without a touchdown or receiving work to go along with his yardage, it was a disappointing fantasy performance. However, his usage is encouraging; the Rams at least trust him enough that they will split Kyren Williams' workload with Corum. It makes him a top-tier handcuff RB, and one that should be rostered in case anything happens to Kyren.

news.body: Blake Corum rushed for 59 yards on 13 carries and caught his lone target for 10 yards in the Rams 37-20 win over the Cardinals.
news.head: Blake Corum sees 14 touches in Week 18 win
news.impact: Corum and Kyren Williams continue to split time in the backfield for the Rams. With the Rams success this season in getting both running backs involved, it should be expected that the rotation continues throughout the team's playoff run.

news.body: Blake Corum (ankle) is officially active for Week 18.
news.head: Blake Corum (ankle) officially active for Week 18
news.impact: Corum exited Monday's game with an ankle injury and was considered questionable to play against Arizona. Corum will continue to work in a rotation with Kyren Williams in the final game of the regular season.

news.body: Breece Hall (thigh) has been ruled out for the New York Jets against the Detroit Lions Sunday.
news.head: Breece Hall (thigh) ruled out Sunday
news.impact: Hall suffered the apparent injury early in the fourth quarter, rushing 13 times for 32 yards while also catching all three of his targets for 23 yards prior to exiting. Braelon Allen will take over No. 1 backfield duties for head coach Aaron Glenn against the Lions.

news.body: Breece Hall carried the ball 16 times for 29 yards while also hauling in each of his five targets for 63 yards in the Jets' 20-17 Week 2 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
news.head: Breece Hall bottled up in Week 2 loss to Packers
news.impact: Hall begins the season as one of the few bright spots in an inconsistent offense, totaling over 90 offensive yards in each of the first two games. The running back remains one of the few reliable options for fantasy managers ahead of a favorable Week 3 matchup against the Detroit Lions.

news.body: Breece Hall carried the ball 22 times for 102 yards and a touchdown while catching both of his targets for 16 yards in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 1.
news.head: Breece Hall finds the end zone in Week 1 win
news.impact: Hall dealt with a groin issue during camp, but he appeared to be at full health in the Week 1 win. The veteran running back handled the majority of the backfield carries, with Braelon Allen mixing in for 10 totes. Hall found the end zone for the first time of the season on a four-yard rush in the third quarter. He will slot in as a solid RB1 in fantasy heading into a Week 2 home matchup against the Packers.

news.body: Breece Hall (groin) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans.
news.head: Breece Hall (groin) off injury report for Sunday
news.impact: Hall is heading into the weekend entirely free of any injury designation ahead of the team's season opener against the Titans on Sunday. He shouldn't have any substantial limitations to his workload in this matchup, and he projects to be a high-quality fantasy asset in this game and beyond if he can stay healthy.

news.body: Bucky Irving ran for 46 yards on 15 carries in the Buccaneers 23-16 loss against the Vikings on Sunday. He also caught 2-of-4 targets for 12 yards receiving.
news.head: Bucky Irving does not play late in game Sunday
news.impact: Irving sat on the sideline for most of the fourth quarter and it is unclear why. There will likely be an update on him early this week. He still saw 15 of the 18 carries for Bucs running backs on the day. He faces a vulnerable Packers defense next week if he is good to go.

news.body: Buccaneers OC Zac Robinson said RB Bucky Irving is on a bit of a pitch count due to the longevity of the season.
news.head: Bucky Irving on 'pitch count' for season per OC Zac Robinson
news.impact: Robinson added he also wants to go with the hot hand in-game. There was some thought going into the season that Kenneth Gainwell could play a bigger role than he has after he got paid in free agency, but Irving has been the clear lead back for Tampa Bay through the first two weeks of the season. This will remain a situation to monitor in the coming weeks.

news.body: Bucky Irving ran for 89 yards on 17 carries in the Buccaneers 23-19 loss against the Browns. He also caught 4-of-4 targets for one yard receiving.
news.head: Bucky Irving totals 21 touches Sunday
news.impact: Irving had one long run of 38 yards, but was otherwise inefficient on the day. He did remain the clear lead back ahead of Kenneth Gainwell. He draws a tough matchup against the Vikings next week.

news.body: Bucky Irving ran for 45 yards and a touchdown on eight carries in the Buccaneers 33-27 loss against the Bengals on Sunday. He also caught 7-of-7 targets for 48 yards receiving.
news.head: Bucky Irving active in passing game Sunday
news.impact: Irving took advantage of the gamescript in the passing game with Tampa Bay falling behind 21-3 early. He also lost a fumble, but otherwise performed well. He will be an RB2 play next week against the Browns.

news.body: Cam Skattebo rushed the ball 12 times for 36 yards and caught four passes for 19 yards in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: Cam Skattebo inefficient in loss Monday
news.impact: Skattebo was pretty well bottled up on Monday night. He was only able to rush for 36 yards at an inefficient clip of 3.0 yards per carry, and he didn't add much in the passing game outside of four receptions. New York's offense as a whole was a mess with injuries in this game, but the young running back will have ample opportunities to bounce back with matchups against the Titans and Cardinals coming up over the next two weeks.

news.body: Cam Skattebo rushed the ball 18 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
news.head: Cam Skattebo leads team in rushing Sunday
news.impact: Skattebo looked pretty solid in his first game back from an injury that ended his 2025 season early. He led the team in rushing yards and scored a touchdown against the Cowboys, and he was clearly the team's top RB in terms of carries, outnumbering the next closest back three to one in that area. He didn't see a single target or catch over the course of the night, however. If Devin Singletary and Tyrone Tracy Jr. continue to serve as the team's primary receiving backs, Skattebo's fantasy ceiling could be capped by that on a week-to-week basis.

news.body: Cam Skattebo participated in Saturday’s practice.
news.head: Cam Skattebo practices Saturday
news.impact: Raanan noted that Skattebo was limited, but seemed fine. He left practice early on Friday following a collision, but it had appeared to be precautionary.

news.body: Cam Skattebo left practice early on Friday.
news.head: Cam Skattebo suffers apparent injury during practice Friday
news.impact: Skattebo went down after a collision with LB Arvell Reese. He remained on the sideline, but didn't return to practice. The Giants will be cautious with him.

news.body: Chase Brown rushed for 61 yards on 13 carries in a 30-27 loss to the Steelers. He caught both of his targets for eight yards.
news.head: Chase Brown quiet in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Brown saw a season low in rushing attempts and targets. Despite the lower volume against Pittsburgh, fantasy managers should expect Brown to remain the workhorse running back for the Bengals in Week 4 against the Jaguars.

news.body: Chase Brown ran for 80 yards on 20 carries in the Bengals 20-6 win over the Texans on Sunday. He also caught 3-of-5 targets for two yards receiving.
news.head: Chase Brown sees 20 carries Sunday
news.impact: Brown did not find the end zone. He ran well, but it was still a fairly quiet day for him overall for fantasy managers. He'll remain an RB1 against the Steelers next week.

news.body: Chase Brown ran for 56 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries in the Bengals 33-27 win over the Buccaneers. He also caught 5-of-6 targets for 22 yards receiving.
news.head: Chase Brown finds the end zone Sunday
news.impact: Brown did not have the most efficient afternoon, but it still got the job done for fantasy managers. He draws a tougher matchup in Week 2 against the Texans.

news.body: The Bengals and RB Chase Brown are reportedly in talks on an extension.
news.head: Chase Brown, Bengals in talks on extension
news.impact: Brown finished the season strong this past year after a rough first half. He is entering the final year of his rookie contract next season, which would make sense for both sides.

news.body: Christian McCaffrey ran for 75 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries in the 49ers 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. He also caught 4-of-5 targets for 41 yards receiving.
news.head: Christian McCaffrey finds the end zone Sunday
news.impact: McCaffrey took over as the clear lead back on Sunday. He found the end zone in the fourth quarter as the Cardinals were making a comeback. He remains a strong RB1 moving forward.

news.body: Christian McCaffrey (rest) did not take part in San Francisco's practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Christian McCaffrey (rest) doesn't practice Wednesday
news.impact: McCaffrey was given Wednesday off as a veteran rest day, which is normal for him at the first practice of the week. He should be a full go for Sunday's game and remains a must-start fantasy option in all league formats for as long as he stays healthy and on the field.

news.body: Christian McCaffrey gained 23 yards on 10 carries and 43 yards on four catches, scoring twice on the ground in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
news.head: Christian McCaffrey finds the end zone twice in Week 2
news.impact: The 49ers' rushing attack was not very efficient in Week 2, but McCaffrey did score a pair of one-yard plunges. As usual, the dual-threat back was also active in the passing game. McCaffrey is up to 29 total touches through two games, averaging 4.6 yards per carry and 7.0 yards per reception. The 49ers appear to be capping the 30-year-old's usage a bit, but he's still a clear RB1, particularly in PPR formats, when healthy.

news.body: Christian McCaffrey (rest) returned to practice for the 49ers as a full participant on Thursday.
news.head: Christian McCaffrey (rest) returns to practice Thursday
news.impact: As expected, McCaffrey returns to being a full participant at practice on Thursday after being given Wednesday off as a veteran rest day. He should be good to go for Week 2 and is primed for a huge workload against the Dolphins, especially now that Kaelon Black (groin) has been added to the injury report for the 49ers.

news.body: Chuba Hubbard ran 12 times for 53 yards in the Panthers' 34-3 win over the Falcons. He also caught both of his targets for 11 yards and a touchdown.
news.head: Chuba Hubbard leads backfield in win over Falcons
news.impact: Hubbard has out-touched the younger Jonathon Brooks, who missed some time in this game due to a groin injury, by a solid margin yet again. He appears to be the back to own in Carolina moving forward. He'll get to play Cleveland next time out.

news.body: Chuba Hubbard carried the ball 10 times for 49 yards and one touchdown while also catching all three of his targets for 38 yards and one touchdown in the Panthers' 59-37 Week 1 loss to the Chicago Bears.
news.head: Chuba Hubbard scores two touchdowns in Week 1 loss to Bears
news.impact: Hubbard took advantage of a primary ball-carrying option before the game script changed, leading the team in rushing yards in the loss. The running back remains a solid option out of the backfield for head coach Dave Canales, with a Week 2 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons up next.

news.body: Chuba Hubbard (hamstring) is off of the injury report ahead of Week 1's matchup against the Chicago Bears.
news.head: Chuba Hubbard (hamstring) off injury report for Week 1
news.impact: Hubbard was battling a hamstring injury earlier this offseason, but it's no longer an issue for him and he carries no injury designation ahead of Week 1. He will likely split work with Jonathan Brooks (groin) in the season opener, which hurts the fantasy outlook for both of them.

news.body: Chuba Hubbard (hamstring) is week-to-week with a hamstring injury per HC Dave Canales. He is expected to play in Week 1.
news.head: Chuba Hubbard (hamstring) week-to-week with hamstring injury
news.impact: While it sounds like Hubbard should be good to go for the season opener, he could still be limited following a multi-week absence. With that said, it’s now wheels up for Jonathon Brooks, who’s now going to see his ADP rise yet again.

news.body: D'Andre Swift rushed 16 times for 45 yards while also hauling in each of his five targets for a team-high 54 yards in the Bears' 9-3 Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
news.head: D'Andre Swift leads quiet offense in Week 2 loss to Vikings
news.impact: Swift continues a solid stretch out of the backfield to begin the season, finishing with over 90 offensive yards in each of the first two games. The running back will look to remain one of the more impactful options in the Chicago offense as the season moves on, with a Week 3 contest against the Philadelphia Eagles up next.

news.body: D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings.
news.head: D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) good to go for Sunday
news.impact: Swift was limited at practice earlier in the week due to a couple of injuries that he was dealing with, but neither of them are serious and he carries no injury designation heading into the weekend. Kyle Monangai (hamstring) is also good to go, so Chicago's backfield should continue operating as usual in a divisional matchup against the Vikings on Sunday.

news.body: D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) was limited at Chicago's practice again on Thursday.
news.head: D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) limited again Thursday
news.impact: The veteran running back was limited for another practice on Thursday, as he is still managing a pair of injuries that are bothering him right now. It doesn't seem likely to affect his availability for Week 2, and fantasy managers shouldn't read much into this issue unless he goes into the weekend with an injury designation.

news.body: D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) was limited at Chicago's practice on Wednesday.
news.head: D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) limited at practice Wednesday
news.impact: Swift is a new addition to Chicago's injury report, being listed with a pair of injuries that left him limited at the team's first practice of the week. They may just be taking a cautious approach with his workload at this point, so it's worth keeping an eye on his status throughout the week, especially with backup Kyle Monangai (hamstring) also on the injury report currently.

news.body: David Montgomery rushed for 33 yards on 11 carries in a 19-17 loss to the Colts. He caught both targets for 15 yards.
news.head: David Montgomery quiet in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Montgomery continues to struggle, tallying 43 rushing yards on 17 carries over the last two games. The veteran also saw Woody Marks come into the game on a short-yardage touchdown run in the forth quarter. Montgomery and the Texans will take on the Cowboys in Week 4.

news.body: David Montgomery ran for 10 yards on six carries in the Texans 20-6 loss against the Bengals on Sunday. He also caught 2-of-2 targets for 14 yards receiving.
news.head: David Montgomery sees just six carries Sunday
news.impact: After a huge Week 1 performance, it was a game to forget for Montgomery and the entire Texans run game. He'll look to bounce back next week against the Colts.

news.body: David Montgomery rushed for 60 yards and two scores on 20 carries, adding three receptions for 19 yards and another touchdown in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.head: David Montgomery has big debut for Texans
news.impact: Montgomery was given 23 touches in his debut with the Texans, as the veteran back was a focal point of the offense. Granted, he only averaged 3.0 yards per carry, but he found the end zone three times while being involved both on the ground and through the air.

news.body: David Montgomery has been traded to the Houston Texans. Houston is sending a fourth rounder, OL Juice Scruggs, and a seventh back to Detroit.
news.head: David Montgomery traded to Houston Texans
news.impact: Montgomery had made it known he wanted a new opportunity given his lack of usage last year, and the Texans came calling. Monty offers a big upgrade over Nick Chubb as the primary thumper, and his ability in the passing game could easily endanger Woody Marks value as well. For dynasty, it’s great for Montgomery and Jahmyr Gibbs managers, while Marks managers will have to deal with a much bigger threat to any potential volume. This also likely means Joe Mixon, who missed all of last season, is done in Houston.

news.body: Derrick Henry rushed for 68 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries in the Ravens 24-17 loss to the Saints. He caught all three of his targets for 19 yards.
news.head: Derrick Henry finds the end zone in Week 2
news.impact: Henry found the end zone on a one-yard rush in the first quarter. The veteran was held in check after that, unable to find any big gains on the ground. Henry and the Ravens will take on Dallas in Week 3.

news.body: Derrick Henry carried the ball 24 times for 144 yards and three touchdowns while also hauling in his lone target for 19 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.head: Derrick Henry rushes for three touchdowns in Week 1 win over Colts
news.impact: Henry capitalized on a sizeable workload out of the Baltimore backfield, averaging an impressive 6.0 yards per carry in the Week 1 win. The superstar running back remains locked in as a reliable RB1 ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.

news.body: Derrick Henry carried the ball 20 times for 126 yards in a 26-24 loss to the Steelers in Week 18.
news.head: Derrick Henry rushes for 126 yards in Week 18
news.impact: Henry was unable to corral his lone target in the contest. With the loss, the Ravens will miss the playoffs in a disappointing ending to the season. Henry finishes the year with 1,595 rushing yards and 16 touchdowns while appearing in all 17 games. He will remain a solid RB1 for fantasy purposes heading into the 2026 season.

news.body: Derrick Henry ran 36 times for 216 yards and four touchdowns in the Ravens' 41-24 win over the Packers on Saturday.
news.head: Derrick Henry has historic night against Packers
news.impact: Henry's performance could easily be what decides the title for many fantasy championships. His 36 rush attempts were a career high in a single game, and his four touchdowns tied his career high in touchdowns in a game. Henry now has over 1,400 rushing yards and 16 touchdowns this season, a great total. The King is still on the throne.

news.body: Dolphins RB De'Von Achane has officially been ruled out for the remainder of Week 3 with a knee injury.
news.head: De'Von Achane (knee) ruled out
news.impact: Achane was tackled awkwardly in the first quarter and was taken to the locker room for further evaluation. Ollie Gordon will handle the primary running back duties for the remainder of the game against the Chiefs. He will finish the day with 17 yards on three carries.

news.body: De’Von Achane (knee) is questionable to return for the Miami Dolphins against the Kansas City Chiefs Sunday according to Ian Rapoport.
news.head: De’Von Achane (knee) questionable to return Sunday
news.impact: Achane suffered the knee injury early in the first quarter, rushing three times for 17 yards prior to exiting. Ollie Gordon II will take over in the backfield against the Chiefs Sunday.

news.body: De'Von Achane gained 74 yards on 20 carries and caught 3-of-6 targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
news.head: De'Von Achane grinds out 93 yards of offense in Week 2
news.impact: Achane's touches went up in Week 2, but his efficiency in the Dolphins' anemic offense was about the same. The dual-threat back has yet to find the end zone through two games while averaging just 3.5 yards per carry. He's best viewed as an RB2 for now, with his volume of touches being the main reason. Achane has a tough matchup coming against the Chiefs.

news.body: De'Von Achane carried the ball 11 times for 36 yards while also hauling in four of his five targets for 30 yards in the Dolphins' 27-13 Week 1 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.head: De'Von Achane sees 15 touches in Week 1 loss to Raiders
news.impact: Achane was unable to find much running room out of the backfield in the season opener, with the Las Vegas defense challenging new starting quarterback Malik Willis to beat it through the air. The running back remains a dynamic option in PPR formats, but fantasy managers may need to temper expectations in the short term, with a Week 2 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers up next.

news.body: Emmett Johnson rushed six times for 17 yards in the Chiefs' 24-10 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 3.
news.head: Emmett Johnson sees six touches in Week 3
news.impact: Johnson has struggled to make an impact out of the backfield to begin the season, finishing with less than 25 rushing yards in each of the first three contests. The running back remains more of a handcuff option for Kenneth Walker owners ahead of a Week 4 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders.

news.body: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Emmett Johnson will continue to get more and more snaps.
news.head: Emmett Johnson expected to continue to see more snaps
news.impact: Reid added that Johnson will see more snaps and take some of the workload off of Kenneth Walker. The rookie has flashed in a limited role over the first two weeks of the season. He remains a solid stash for fantasy managers in his current role.

news.body: Emmett Johnson rushed the ball two times for 25 yards and caught two passes for 20 yards in Sunday's 33-30 OT win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.head: Emmett Johnson a non-factor Sunday
news.impact: The Chiefs didn't give Johnson much work in their close overtime win on Sunday night. He saw just four touches over the course of the game, but he was still able to turn that into an efficient 35 yards. He shouldn't be considered much more than a handcuff fantasy option at this point in the season.

news.body: Emmett Johnson rushed the ball eight times for 24 yards and caught two passes for 44 yards in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Emmett Johnson totals 68 yards in NFL debut Monday
news.impact: The rookie looked good in his NFL debut on Monday night, totaling 68 yards on ten opportunities against one of the NFL's best defensive fronts. Kenneth Walker III is clearly the bellcow running back on this offense, but it looks like Johnson has solidified himself as the RB2 and will continue to play an important depth role for the Chiefs over the course of the season.

news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for 43 yards on 12 carries and caught his lone target for five yards in the loss to Dallas Sunday.
news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt sees 12 carries in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Croskey-Merritt was out targeted by Rachaad White 6-to-1, but each tallied 43 yards on the ground. The Commanders' offense took a massive blow losing Jayden Daniels to a dislocated elbow, so the running game will likely be relied upon more heading into Week 3.

news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt carried the ball 16 times for 63 yards and one touchdown while also catching his only target for a loss of seven yards in the Commanders’ 24-22 Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt reaches end zone in Week 1 loss
news.impact: Croskey-Merritt made the most of his opportunities out of the backfield, accounting for 50% of the carries for the Commanders in Week 1. The running back seems poised to receive as much volume as he can handle as the primary option out of the backfield to begin the season for head coach Dan Quinn, with a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Dallas Cowboys up next.

news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) will play in Week 1 for the Washington Commanders against the Philadelphia Eagles according to Ian Rapoport.
news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) will play in Week 1

news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) limited participant Wednesday
news.impact: Croskey-Merritt is managing a groin injury right now and was unable to log a full practice session on Wednesday as a result. There's an off-chance that it will leave him sidelined for Week 1, which would lead to more work for Rachaad White against the Eagles.

news.body: Jadarian Price (chest) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Washington Commanders.
news.head: Jadarian Price (chest) good to go for Sunday
news.impact: The rookie will be good to go for Week 3, as he currently carries no injury designation heading into the weekend. He will have an easy matchup against the Commanders this week, but his upside may be limited by Emmanuel Wilson if he sees a lot of opportunities again this week.

news.body: Jadarian Price was limited in practice on Thursday.
news.head: Jadarian Price (chest) limited in practice Thursday
news.impact: Price has been limited in practice on back-to-back days to begin the week. His status will need to be monitored in practice on Friday.

news.body: Jadarian Price (chest) was officially a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Jadarian Price (chest) officially limited Wednesday
news.impact: The rookie was a limited participant in the team's first practice of the week on Wednesday. He recently suffered a chest injury, and it remains unclear whether or not it will force him to miss time. Look for George Holani (knee) to see more work if Price misses any time.

news.body: Jadarian Price ran 13 times for 52 yards and caught one of two targets for eight yards in the Seahawks' 31-7 win over Arizona on Sunday.
news.head: Jadarian Price sees 14 touches in win
news.impact: Price tied with Cooper Kupp for third in targets on the Seahawks, but with it being just two targets, that's not saying much. He was behind Emanuel Wilson this week in rushing as well, who had 21 carries of his own. Price has been involved, but not featured so far through two weeks, very reminiscent of his days at Notre Dame. It'll be tough to start him outside of a flex play until he either shows more or is fed more work.

news.body: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 99 yards and two touchdowns on 20 carries in a 31-24 win over the Jets. He caught 7-of-8 targets for 65 yards and a touchdown.
news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs tallies three touchdowns in Week 3 win
news.impact: Gibbs continues to impress this season, tallying six touchdowns in his first three games of the season. He caught an 11-yard pass in the fourth quarter to put the Lions on top of the Jets to seal the win. Gibbs and the Lions will take on the Panthers in Week 4.

news.body: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed the ball 16 times for 52 yards and caught 6-of-8 targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in Thursday night's 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs plays well in loss Thursday
news.impact: Thursday's game wasn't great for Gibbs in terms of efficiency, but he was still able to accumulate over 100 yards and a touchdown on Thursday night, which left him with a great fantasy total in this shootout matchup against the Bills. He will continue to be a top-tier fantasy option at the RB position for the remainder of the season, provided he remains healthy for most of it.

news.body: Jahmyr Gibbs carried the ball 29 times for 156 yards and two touchdowns while also hauling in all five of his targets for 30 yards in the Lions' 31-30 Week 1 win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs leads backfield attack in Week 1 win over Saints
news.impact: Gibbs was dynamic out of the backfield for head coach Dan Campbell, averaging 5.4 yards per carry in the win. The running back remains an explosive RB1 option in all formats, with a Week 2 road matchup against the Buffalo Bills up next.

news.body: Jahmyr Gibbs has agreed to 3-year, $67.5 million deal with Lions that could be worth up to $75.75 million. Gibbs is now the NFL’s highest paid running back.
news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs agrees to 3-year, $67.5 million deal with Lions
news.impact: Gibbs has done everything he needs to to earn this money. He’s a premier running back in the NFL, in the argument for the best. Now with David Montgomery gone, we will see how well he can shoulder a workhorse role, and fantasy managers are rightly expecting big things.

news.body: James Cook III carried the ball 24 times for 154 yards and one touchdown with one fumble lost in the Bills' 24-16 Week 3 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: James Cook III dominates on ground in Week 3 win over Chargers
news.impact: Cook III has been dynamic out of the backfield of late, rushing for over 130 yards with one touchdown in each of the last two contests. The running back remains an explosive RB1 option in all formats ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the New England Patriots.

news.body: James Cook III rushed the ball 21 times for 135 yards and a touchdown in Thursday night's 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions.
news.head: James Cook III plays well in win Thursday
news.impact: Buffalo's offense was firing on all cylinders on Thursday night, and that included Cook. He rushed for 135 yards at an efficient clip of 6.5 yards per carry on the night and was able to get into the end zone on one of those carries. He wasn't very involved in the passing game, but he still dominated the backfield and was the only running back to receive even a single opportunity for the Bills.

news.body: James Cook III ran 13 times for 57 yards and caught three of four targets for 12 yards in the Bills’ 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday.
news.head: James Cook III goes for 69 yards in big win over Texans
news.impact: Cook was fine on his touches and was saved by his three receptions in PPR formats, but it fantasy managers will be hoping for more. He’s still a premium running back, and he will get his chance early this week as the Bills play the Lions on Thursday night.

news.body: James Cook III and all Bills starters are set to play Saturday, per HC Joe Brady.
news.head: James Cook will play in preseason opener
news.impact: Cook is reportedly expected to have a larger role as a pass catcher in 2026. Saturday's preseason opener against the Panthers could offer a preview of the Bills' plans for their RB1.

news.body: Javonte Williams rushed for 30 yards on 12 carries in the Cowboys 37-20 win over the Commanders. He caught 3-of-4 targets for 20 yards.
news.head: Javonte Williams sees 15 touches in Week 2
news.impact: Williams struggled to get anything consistent going against the Commanders' rush defense. Williams has logged 12 carries in both games this season, but has failed to get anything consistent going yardage wise. Williams and the Cowboys will take on the Ravens in Week 3.

news.body: Javonte Williams rushed the ball 12 times for 41 yards and a touchdown and caught five passes for 31 yards and another touchdown in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the New York Giants.
news.head: Javonte Williams scores twice in loss Sunday
news.impact: Williams was arguably Dallas' most impactful offensive player on Sunday night. He scored two touchdowns and totaled 72 yards on a night where the entire offense struggled, leaving him with a surprisingly good fantasy total on the week. He is clearly the team's bellcow running back at this point and should be viewed as a high quality fantasy option for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Javonte Williams remains as Dallas’ lead back by a comfortable margin headed into 2026 following a breakout campaign that ended with him signing a three year extension with the team.
news.head: Javonte Williams remains Cowboys lead back in 2026
news.impact: Williams has the bell-cow, or at least the lead role, on lockdown. However, what’s primarily in question is who will be backing him up, as Jaydon Blue, Malik Davis, and Phil Mafah are all vying for the role. It appears Dallas, while comfortable with Williams, doesn’t want to put the same sort of workload on him again this season as he had in 2025. That could hurt his upside unless he becomes more proficient in the passing game, but on volume alone he should maintain RB2 status.

news.body: Javonte Williams has landed a three year deal with the Dallas Cowboys, with $16 million guaranteed.
news.head: Javonte Williams lands three year deal with Dallas
news.impact: The former Bronco cashes in after a big season in Dallas. Expectations were fairly low for the veteran back, who was coming off of multiple injuries and disappointing seasons, but he crushed expectations to the tune of 1,200 rushing yards and 11 rushing touchdowns. He is a strong RB2 heading into 2026 with RB1 upside.

news.body: Jaylen Warren rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries in a 30-27 win over the Bengals. He caught 3-of-4 targets for 49 yards.
news.head: Jaylen Warren excellent in Week 3 win
news.impact: Warren averaged 7.5 yards per carry and he dominated the rushing attempts with Rico Dowdle (toe) inactive Sunday. With the Steelers taking on the Browns on Thursday, Warren could be in line for a similar workload if Dowdle is unable to play.

news.body: Steelers RB Jaylen Warren (shoulder) is officially active for a Week 3 matchup with the Bengals.
news.head: Jaylen Warren (shoulder) officially active for Week 3
news.impact: Warren was limited in practice throughout the week but will play and start against the Bengals. With Rico Dowdle (toe) inactive, Warren could be in line for a workhorse role in Week 3.

news.body: Jaylen Warren (shoulder) is expected to play on Sunday against the Bengals after being listed with a shoulder injury this week. He was able to get some limited practice sessions in later in the week, and is likely good to go.
news.head: Jaylen Warren (shoulder) expected to play against Cincy
news.impact: Fellow RB Rico Dowdle is out for the game, so Warren’s availability is crucial for the team that lacks an experienced back behind him. He should be an RB2 with upside thanks to his pass catching skillset.

news.body: Jaylen Warren (shoulder) will be questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals.
news.head: Jaylen Warren (shoulder) questionable to play Sunday
news.impact: Warren is still not 100% healthy at this point and officially carries a questionable tag heading into the weekend due to the shoulder injury that he's dealing with. He will likely be a great fantasy option this week if he's cleared to play without any major restrictions, however, as the team has already ruled out Rico Dowdle (toe) for this divisional matchup.

news.body: Jeremiyah Love ran for 90 yards on 21 carries in the Cardinals 36-30 loss against the 49ers on Sunday. He also caught 5-of-5 targets for 19 yards receiving and a touchdown.
news.head: Jeremiyah Love has career day Sunday
news.impact: Love totaled a career-high 26 touches. It was the first game so far where he clearly out-snapped Tyler Allgeier. He'll look to continue the workhorse role into next week against the Giants.

news.body: Jeremiyah Love ran nine times for 29 yards and caught three passes for 16 yards in the Cardinals' 31-7 loss to Seattle.
news.head: Jeremiyah Love struggles in loss to Seattle
news.impact: Like the rest of the Cardinals' offense, Love struggled to move the ball against the Seahawks' stout defense. He will face yet another tough matchup next week, as Arizona takes on San Francisco.

news.body: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is off of Arizona's injury report ahead of their Week 2 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks.
news.head: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) off injury report for Week 2
news.impact: The rookie running back was dealing with an ankle injury prior to the team's season opener last week, but he was able to play through it against the Chargers and should be able to do the same in Week 2 now that he's off of the injury report entirely. His workload should continue to ramp up in the coming weeks if he can stay healthy.

news.body: Jeremiyah Love picked up 41 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.head: Jeremiyah Love finds the end zone in debut
news.impact: Love added a pair of grabs for nine yards to his NFL debut, and despite still being somewhat limited by the ankle sprain he sustained a month ago, the rookie certainly showed promise of things to come. Tyler Allgeier did get six more carries than Love, but that load share should begin to swing the other way as the season moves forward. The Cardinals have a tough matchup with the Seahawks on tap for Week 2.

news.body: J.K. Dobbins (hip) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: J.K. Dobbins (hip) good to go for Sunday
news.impact: The veteran running back is going to be able to play on Sunday, which was the expectation after he was able to practice in full on Thursday and Friday. RJ Harvey (hamstring) is set to make his return to the timeline, but it's likely that the veteran will continue to serve as the team's primary rusher and goal-line threat for the foreseeable future.

news.body: J.K. Dobbins (hip) logged a full practice session on Thursday.
news.head: J.K. Dobbins (hip) logs full practice session Thursday
news.impact: Dobbins is expected to be good to go for Week 3 after being upgraded to a full participant at practice on Thursday. RJ Harvey (hamstring) was also able to practice in full, but rookie Jonah Coleman (ankle) was absent, so it looks like Denver's backfield is still expected to be at less than full strength in Week 3.

news.body: J.K. Dobbins (hip) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: J.K. Dobbins (hip) limited at practice Wednesday
news.impact: Dobbins was a officially a limited participant for the Broncos on Wednesday due to a hip injury that he recently suffered. It looks like he will have a good chance to play through it in Week 3, and he will be primed for more work than usual if one or both of RJ Harvey (hamstring) and Jonah Coleman (ankle) are sidelined against the Rams on Sunday night.

news.body: J.K. Dobbins (hamstring) was seen practicing for the Broncos on Wednesday.
news.head: J.K. Dobbins (hamstring) seen practicing Wednesday
news.impact: Dobbins was seen at practice on Wednesday after recently suffering a minor hamstring injury of some kind. It looks like he may be well enough to play through it in Week 3, but it's too early to say for sure. RJ Harvey (hamstring) and Jonah Coleman (ankle) both seem to be trending the right way as well, which may lead to a crowded backfield for Denver this week.

news.body: Jonathan Taylor rushed for 68 yards on 23 carries in a 19-17 win over Houston. He caught 2-of-3 targets for four yards.
news.head: Jonathan Taylor held in check in Week 3 win
news.impact: Taylor continues to receive plenty of touches in the Colts' offense this season, but struggled to make the most of them in Week 3. His 72 total yards are a season low for Taylor. He will look to bounce back against the Commanders in Week 4.

news.body: Jonathan Taylor rushed the ball 24 times for 92 yards and two touchdowns while adding four receptions for 40 yards through the air in Sunday night's 33-30 OT loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.head: Jonathan Taylor scores twice in overtime loss Sunday
news.impact: Taylor was the engine for Indianapolis' offense on Sunday night. He totaled 132 yards over the course of the night and was able to score two touchdowns on the ground. He has been very strong to start the season and should continue to be considered an elite fantasy option for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Jonathan Taylor carried the ball 19 times for 98 yards and two touchdowns while also catching three of his four targets for 23 yards in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 1.
news.head: Jonathan Taylor rushes for two touchdowns in Week 1 loss
news.impact: Taylor was the lone bright spot in an underwhelming Colts offense to begin the season, averaging 5.2 yards per carry in the loss. The superstar running back will look to remain an impactful backfield option in Week 2 against the Kansas City Chiefs.

news.body: Jonathan Taylor has agreed to a two-year, $44 million deal with the Indianapolis Colts that could be worth up to $47 million.
news.head: Jonathan Taylor agrees to two-year, $44 million extension with Colts
news.impact: The 27 year old is coming off of back-to-back 1,400 yard rushing seasons with at least 11 rushing touchdowns in each, including a ridiculous 18 rushing touchdowns in 2025. Taylor should be viewed as a top tier running back in 2026, and his deal secures his dynasty value for the next several seasons.

news.body: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs had his initial court appearance moved up to Sept. 10 from Nov. 17 regarding Jacobs' misdemeanor charges.
news.head: Josh Jacobs has court appearance date moved up
news.impact: Jacobs was charged with battery and criminal destruction of property and is scheduled to appear at the Brown County courthouse on Sept. 10, multiple days before Green Bay's season opener against Minnesota. It is unclear how this will affect his return timeline; Jacobs is currently on the commissioner's exempt list, with a potential suspension looming.

news.body: Packers GM Brian Gutekunst said he expected Josh Jacobs to play for the team in 2026.
news.head: Josh Jacobs expected to play for Packers in 2026 per GM
news.impact: Gutekunst said he wants to let the process play out when asked if there’s a scenario in which the Packers release Jacobs. He was placed on the Commissioners Exempt List on Sunday. This will remain a situation to monitor.

news.body: Josh Jacobs has been placed on the commissioner exempt list by the National Football League according to Tom Pelissero.
news.head: Josh Jacobs placed on commissioner of exempt list
news.impact: Jacobs is now ineligible to practice or play for the Packers while the league continues their investigation into alleged improper behavior while being charged with two misdemeanors related to his conduct earlier in the week. If the running back is forced to sit out for any period of the regular season, MarShawn Lloyd will be in line to receive the majority of backfield work while the recently acquired Kaleb Johnson gets up to speed on the offensive playbook with Week 1 approaching.

news.body: Josh Jacobs has been charged with two misdemeanors following an incident in May. His initial court date is set for mid-November. The NFL is conducting its own investigation, and a suspension could soon follow.
news.head: Josh Jacobs charged with two misdemeanors stemming from May incident
news.impact: It's important to remember that the NFL has the ability to either suspend Jacobs at the start of the season or wait until the legal process is over. If they wait, then Jacobs will likely not face suspension until next year. If not, we could be looking at a potential 6-8 game absence, though that is more of an educated guess at this point. For anyone taking Jacobs in drafts right now, Marshawn Lloyd is a must-have handcuff and is a great target for Zero-RB builds.

news.body: Kaelon Black ran for 17 yards on four carries in the 49ers 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
news.head: Kaelon Black quiet Sunday
news.impact: Black saw one target which he didn't haul in. Christian McCaffrey took over as the clear lead back on the afternoon. Black remains a stash for fantasy managers.

news.body: Kaelon Black gained 25 yards on seven carries in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
news.head: Kaelon Black gets seven carries in Week 2
news.impact: After gaining 65 yards on 14 carries in Week 1, Black saw his attempts cut in half in Week 2. The 49ers' rushing attack was not very efficient in Sunday's win, but Brock Purdy more than made up for that with his passing prowess. Black has gained 90 yards on 21 carries through two games, and he maintains decent fantasy value as the backup to Christian McCaffrey.

news.body: Kaelon Black (groin) is active for Week 2 for the San Francisco 49ers against the Miami Dolphins according to Nick Wagoner.
news.head: Kaelon Black (groin) active for Week 2
news.impact: Black is good to go after not experiencing any setbacks during pregame warmups for head coach Kyle Shanahan, offering another dynamic option alongside Christian McCaffrey out of the San Francisco backfield against the Dolphins Sunday.

news.body: Kaelon Black (groin) is expected to play on Sunday against the Dolphins.
news.head: Kaelon Black (groin) expected to play on Sunday
news.impact: If Black plays it seems unlikely he'll have the 50-50 split with Christian McCaffrey he had last time out, and likely will play a more complementary role. However, if the Niners do get up big, he could see a decent amount of touches, so he could be flex-worthy in deep formats.

news.body: Kaleb Johnson ran four times for six yards and caught one of three targets for 10 yards in the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons.
news.head: Kaleb Johnson goes for 16 scrimmage yards in loss
news.impact: Johnson had just as many carries as Marshawn Lloyd, but half the yards. He's not doing enough at this point to warrant taking over the backfield, so expect a split to continue.

news.body: Kaleb Johnson rushed eight times for 32 yards in the Packers' 20-17 Week 2 win over the New York Jets.
news.head: Kaleb Johnson leads ground attack in Week 2 win
news.impact: Johnson made the most of modest involvement in his first game action of the season, averaging 4.0 yards per carry in the win. The running back could be in line for an increased workload as part of a difficult Green Bay backfield for fantasy managers to trust, with a Week 3 contest against the Atlanta Falcons up next.

news.body: Kaleb Johnson is being traded to the Green Bay Packers by the Pittsburgh Steelers according to Tom Pelissero.
news.head: Kaleb Johnson traded to Packers
news.impact: Details of the trade are still being finalized between the two organizations, with Johnson receiving the fresh start the running back desperately needs after falling out of favor in a Pittsburgh backfield that will be led by the duo of Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle this upcoming season. Johnson’s role should become clearer as the National Football League continues their investigation into No. 1 running back Josh Jacobs, potentially resulting in a backup opportunity behind current No. 2 option MarShawn Lloyd.

news.body: Steelers HC Mike McCarthy told reporters, “everybody has a clean slate and let’s get to work,” when asked about RB Kaleb Johnson.
news.head: Kaleb Johnson given 'clean slate'
news.impact: The former third-round pick had an extremely underwhelming rookie campaign, carrying the ball 28 times for 69 yards across 10 appearances. Entering 2026, he sits behind both Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle on the team’s depth chart. His path to fantasy relevance will be very difficult unless he stands out in training camp.

news.body: Kenneth Walker III carried the ball 18 times for 70 yards and one touchdown while also catching both of his targets for three yards and one touchdown in the Chiefs' 24-10 Week 3 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Kenneth Walker III reaches end zone twice in Week 3 win over Dolphins
news.impact: Walker III has gotten off to an impactful start to the season out of the Kansas City backfield, recording multiple touchdowns in two of the first three contests. The running back remains a dynamic option as part of a revamped Chiefs offensive attack for head coach Andy Reid, with a Week 4 divisional matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders up next.

news.body: Kenneth Walker III rushed the ball 24 times for 117 yards and caught 6-of-10 targets for 61 yards in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.head: Kenneth Walker III totals 178 yards in OT win Sunday
news.impact: Walker's hot start to the season continued on Sunday night. He totaled 178 yards from scrimmage in a big win over the Colts, and he was able to do that while maintaining terrific efficiency. He will continue to be a top-tier fantasy asset for as long as he remains healthy and on the field moving forward.

news.body: Kenneth Walker III rushed the ball 23 times for 173 yards and a touchdown while catching 3-of-6 targets for 18 yards and an additional touchdown in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Kenneth Walker III dominant in win Monday
news.impact: Walker was absolutely dominant in his debut with the Chiefs on Monday night. He totaled 191 yards and two touchdowns over the course of the game, which was especially impressive considering that he did it against one of the best defenses in the NFL in the Broncos. He looks great on his new offense and should be in line for a huge season if he can stay healthy with this increased workload.

news.body: Kenneth Walker III (foot) is off of the injury report ahead of Monday night's game against the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Kenneth Walker III (foot) off injury report for Monday
news.impact: Walker was previously dealing with a foot injury of some kind, but he is over it now and is no longer listed on the team's injury report ahead of their Week 1 matchup against the Broncos. Fantasy managers should expect him to be highly involved on Monday night, although the tough matchup may hurt his ceiling from a fantasy perspective.

news.body: Kenny Gainwell ran for -4 yards on three carries in the Buccaneers 23-16 loss against the Vikings on Sunday. He also caught 2-of-5 targets for 14 yards receiving.
news.head: Kenny Gainwell quiet again Sunday
news.impact: Gainwell was once again not involved much. It is worth noting Bucky Irving was on the sideline for most of the final quarter. The status of Irving will need to be monitored this week.

news.body: Kenny Gainwell ran for 10 yards on two carries in the Buccaneers 23-19 loss against the Browns. He also caught 3-of-4 targets for five yards receiving.
news.head: Kenny Gainwell remains in limited role Sunday
news.impact: Bucky Irving was the clear lead back for the second straight week. Gainwell remains a pure stash for fantasy managers in his current role.

news.body: Kenny Gainwell ran for 15 yards on five carries in the Buccaneers 33-27 loss against the Bengals on Sunday. He also caught his line target for three yards receiving.
news.head: Kenny Gainwell uninvolved Sunday
news.impact: This felt like the perfect time for Gainwell to make an impact with Tampa Bay falling behind 21-3 early, but it was Bucky Irving in the passing game out of the backfield who caught seven passes. Gainwell is a risky flex play for now in PPR leagues until we see him more involved.

news.body: Kenny Gainwell is not practicing on Friday due to personal reasons.
news.head: Kenny Gainwell (personal) not practicing Friday, expected back Sunday
news.impact: It is an excused absence for Gainwell, who is expected to be back on Sunday. He is competing for a complimentary role alongside Bucky Irving.

news.body: Kyle Monangai (knee) practiced in a full capacity on Friday.
news.head: Kyle Monangai (knee) practices in full Friday
news.impact: The young running back was able to return to practice in a full capacity on Friday after being absent on Thursday due to a knee issue of some kind. He should be a full go for Monday night's game but isn't expected to be a worthwhile fantasy option with Chicago likely to be down to their third-string quarterback for that matchup.

news.body: Kyle Monangai (knee) didn't take part in Chicago's practice on Thursday.
news.head: Kyle Monangai (knee) doesn't practice Thursday
news.impact: Monangai missed Chicago's first practice of the week on Thursday. He's dealing with a knee injury right now and is considered day-to-day for the time being. It looks likely that he will be available to play on Monday night, though that is far from certain at this point.

news.body: Bears RB Kyle Monangai was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
news.head: Kyle Monangai not seen practicing Wednesday
news.impact: The Bears are on a Monday Night Football schedule so the first injury report of the week comes out. Cronin notes that Monangai was in the injury tent in the second half against Minnesota.

news.body: Kyle Monangai rushed 10 times for 47 yards while also catching both of his targets for 11 yards in the Bears' 9-3 Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
news.head: Kyle Monangai leads backfield in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Monangai struggled to make an impact against a strong Minnesota rushing defense, finishing with less than 50 rushing yards in the loss. The running back will look to get back on track in Week 3 against the Philadelphia Eagles.

news.body: Kyren Williams rushed the ball 12 times for 85 yards and caught two passes for 12 yards and a touchdown in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
news.head: Kyren Williams finds end zone Monday
news.impact: Williams had a productive night on Monday. He led the team in rushing and fell just three yards shy of the 100-total yards mark over the course of the game, and he was also able to haul in a touchdown to put the cherry on top. Concerns still exist for his season-long outlook, though, with Blake Corum seeing just one less touch on the night and seemingly only getting better and better.

news.body: Kyren Williams ran 11 times for 41 yards and the Rams' only touchdown. He also caught all three of his targets for 24 receiving yards.
news.head: Kyren Williams punches in score in loss to Niners
news.impact: Williams' day was saved by the touchdown; otherwise it was fairly miserable. Blake Corum showed out in his opportunities, but he was limited to ground work only. Kyren appears to be in a committee now, but he at least has the edge in passing situations, giving him more appeal.

news.body: Kyren Williams rushed for 60 yards on 12 carries in the Rams 37-20 win over the Cardinals. He caught 3-of-5 targets for 21 yards.
news.head: Kyren Williams sees 15 touches in Week 18 win
news.impact: Williams and Blake Corum continued to split time in the backfield to close out the regular season. Both running backs have been effective in that role this season, so the Rams will likely continue that throughout their playoff run.

news.body: Rams RB Kyren Williams (ankle) is officially active for Week 18.
news.head: Kyren Williams (ankle) officially active for Week 18
news.impact: Williams was limited in practice this week, but is healthy enough to suit up against the Cardinals. Despite having a playoff spot locked up, the Rams are playing their starters in the final regular season game.

news.body: MarShawn Lloyd ran four times for 11 yards and caught two of three targets for seven yards in the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons.
news.head: MarShawn Lloyd snags two passes in loss
news.impact: Lloyd wasn't all that impressive in this game, but he was better than Kaleb Johnson this time out. The backfield is a mess right now with Josh Jacobs out, and everyone is struggling to run. Expect both Lloyd and Johnson to be irrelevant for fantasy moe often than not.

news.body: MarShawn Lloyd rushed six times for 20 yards while also hauling in both of his targets for six yards and one touchdown in the Packers' 20-17 Week 2 win over the New York Jets.
news.head: MarShawn Lloyd catches touchdown in quiet Week 2 performance
news.impact: Lloyd has underwhelmed despite increased touches out of the Green Bay backfield to begin the season, finishing with less than 40 rushing yards in each of the first two games. The running back remains a risky option as part of a running back group leaving a lot to be desired, with a Week 3 contest against the Atlanta Falcons up next.

news.body: MarShawn Lloyd ran for 37 yards on 13 carries in the Packers 39-22 loss against the Vikings. He did not catch his lone target.
news.head: MarShawn Lloyd sees 13 carries Sunday
news.impact: Lloyd was the lead back in the Packers backfield without Josh Jacobs. He was very inefficient as he averaged less than three yards per carry. He'll be a flex play next week against the Jets.

news.body: Packers OC Adam Stenavich confirmed that MarShawn Lloyd will play in the preseason.
news.head: MarShawn Lloyd will play in preseason
news.impact: Stenavich said every day Lloyd is able to practice, he gets more confident his injury issues are fully behind him. He is competing the backup role in the Packers backfield.

news.body: Omarion Hampton carried the ball 15 times for 56 yards while also failing to catch his lone target in the Chargers' 24-16 Week 3 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Omarion Hampton leads ground attack in Week 3 loss to Bills
news.impact: Hampton struggled to find consistent running room Sunday, rushing for less than 60 yards for the second time in the first three contests. The running back remains one of the more reliable options as part of an inconsistent Chargers offense to begin the season, with a Week 4 contest against the Seattle Seahawks up next.

news.body: Omarion Hampton rushed the ball 23 times for 94 yards and a touchdown and caught two passes for 21 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.head: Omarion Hampton scores once in loss Sunday
news.impact: Hampton was one of the lone bright spots for the Chargers on Sunday. He logged 115 total yards and found the end zone once over the course of the afternoon, though he left something to be desired in the passing game. He should continue to be a good fantasy option moving forward, though the present struggles of Los Angeles' offense may cap his upside from a fantasy perspective.

news.body: Omarion Hampton rushed for 43 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
news.head: Omarion Hampton finds the end zone in Week 1 loss
news.impact: A first-round pick in 2025, Hampton carried quite a bit of hype coming into his second NFL season, as did the Chargers' offense as a whole. At least some of that hype immediately died down after a disappointing season debut against a suspect Arizona defense, but it is only one game under new OC Mike McDaniel. Hampton found the end zone on an eight-yard run in the opening quarter, and this Chargers' attack will find its footing at some point. The Raiders are up next.

news.body: Omarion Hampton is not practicing on Wednesday.
news.head: Omarion Hampton (ankle) will not practice Wednesday
news.impact: Hampton is “working through it” and “doing everything he can” to get the ankle better that sidelined him in Week 18. He should still play in the Wild Card round against the Patriots, but it is possible he's still fighting through the injury.

news.body: Quinshon Judkins is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
news.head: Quinshon Judkins (personal) off injury report Sunday
news.impact: Judkins landed on the injury report for personal reasons this week. He'll remain an RB2 off volume this week for fantasy managers.

news.body: Quinshon Judkins (personal) was limited at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Quinshon Judkins (personal) limited at practice on Thursday
news.impact: The young running back was a limited participant at practice on Thursday due to a personal issue of some kind. It doesn't seem likely to threaten his availability for Sunday's game, but we won't know more for sure until later on in the week.

news.body: Quinshon Judkins ran for 21 yards on 12 carries in the Browns 23-19 win over the Buccaneers. He also caught 5-of-5 targets for 27 yards receiving.
news.head: Quinshon Judkins sees 17 touches Sunday
news.impact: Judkins was shut down on the ground, but somewhat salvaged his day in the passing game for fantasy managers in PPR leagues. His upside remains limited given his situation.

news.body: Quinshon Judkins ran 12 times for 33 yards in the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday. He also caught both of his targets for 17 yards.
news.head: Quinshon Judkins quiet in blowout loss to Jaguars
news.impact: Judkins was held back by the Browns inept offensive showing, as everyone except Deshaun Watson and Denzel Boston was held under 10 PPR points, and those two got over that because of a bomb touchdown in garbage time. Judkins is the lead back, but his fantasy value is highly questionable unless something changes.

news.body: Commanders RB Rachaad White is questionable to return Sunday due to a shoulder injury.
news.head: Rachaad White (shoulder) questionable to return
news.impact: White had four rushing yards on two carries and one receptions for six yards prior to the injury. Jacory Croskey-Merritt will continue to see the bulk of the carries with White sidelined.

news.body: Rachaad White rushed for 43 yards on seven carries in the Commanders loss to the Cowboys. He caught 6-of-6 targets for 40 yards.
news.head: Rachaad White hauls in six passes in Week 2 loss
news.impact: White saw six targets to Jacory Croskey-Merritt's one target, but both contributed the same amount of yards on the ground. With Jayden Daniels (elbow) out for the foreseeable future, the running game should get more of a focus heading into a Week 3 matchup with Seattle.

news.body: Rachaad White rushed seven times for 22 yards while also catching both of his targets for five yards in the Commanders’ 24-22 Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.head: Rachaad White sees nine touches in Week 1
news.impact: White made the most of modest touches in the season-opening contest, finishing second to Jacory Croskey-Merritt in touches in the loss. The running back offers more value in PPR formats as the No. 2 backfield option for the Commanders, with a Week 2 contest against the Dallas Cowboys up next.

news.body: Rachaad White (hamstring) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.head: Rachaad White (hamstring) off injury report for Sunday
news.impact: The veteran running back is fully over his hamstring injury at this point and is set to be a full go for Washington's season opener on Sunday. He will be primed for more work if Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is limited or sidelined for the team's matchup against the Eagles.

news.body: Patriots RB Rhamondre Stevenson tallied 43 rushing yards on six carries in the Patriots' 20-3 win over the Steelers. He caught 1-of-2 targets for three yards.
news.head: Rhamondre Stevenson limited to six carries in Week 2
news.impact: Stevenson saw the majority of the carries go to TreVeyon Henderson after Stevenson fumbled the ball in the first quarter. Stevenson struggled with fumbles in 2025 and that could impact his usage moving forward if he is unable to improve his ball security. Stevenson and the Patriots will take on the Jaguars in Week 3.

news.body: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed the ball 18 times for 51 yards and caught five passes for 44 yards in Wednesday night's 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
news.head: Rhamondre Stevenson totals 95 yards Wednesday
news.impact: Stevenson was New England's workhorse running back on Wednesday night with TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) out of the lineup. He ran at an inefficient clip of 2.8 yards per carry on the night, but his fantasy total was saved by the fact that he caught five passes. He will be more efficient than this in the future but will lose passing work to Henderson when he's back, so he will likely continue to be touchdown dependent on a week-to-week basis.

news.body: Rhamondre Stevenson is questionable to return to Sunday's Divisional Round game against the Texans.
news.head: Rhamondre Stevenson (eye) questionable to return Sunday
news.impact: Stevenson left the game early with a eye injury. TreVeyon Henderson should see more snaps in the Patriots backfield while he is sidelined.

news.body: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed the ball seven times for 131 yards and two touchdowns and caught two passes for 22 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-10 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Rhamondre Stevenson dominant in Week 18 win
news.impact: Stevenson saw just nine touches over the course of the afternoon on Sunday, but that was all that he needed. He logged 150+ total yards and three touchdowns against Miami, which left him with a dominant fantasy total in that matchup. He is set to return to New England next season and will continue to be featured in a two-headed backfield with TreVeyon Henderson.

news.body: Rico Dowdle (toe) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals.
news.head: Rico Dowdle (toe) ruled out for Sunday
