news.impact: Dowdle is not going to be available to play on Sunday, as he is dealing with a toe injury right now and will need at least a week off in order to rest and recover from it. Fantasy managers should expect Jaylen Warren (shoulder) to see the bulk of the work for the Steelers if he's active this week.

news.body: Rico Dowdle did not practice on Thursday.
news.head: Rico Dowdle (toe) absent from practice Thursday
news.impact: Dowdle was seen in a boot during practice on Wednesday. He is likely to be ruled out this week. Jaylen Warren should enter Sunday's game in a clear lead role.

news.body: Rico Dowdle was wearing a boot on his right foot during practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Rico Dowdle (toe) in boot Wednesday
news.impact: Dowdle left last week's game early with what was reported as a toe injury. He remains day-to-day.

news.body: Steelers RB Rico Dowdle is considered day-to-day with a toe injury.
news.head: Rico Dowdle (toe) day-to-day
news.impact: Dowdle was carted to the locker room on Sunday with the injury. He checked out "relatively OK" following tests.

news.body: RJ Harvey (hamstring) will play in Sunday night's game against the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: RJ Harvey (hamstring) will play Sunday
news.impact: Harvey is set to make his return to the field in Week 3 after being sidelined for one game due to a hamstring issue. He should see a full workload against the Rams this week, especially with rookie Jonah Coleman (ankle) set to be sidelined in that matchup.

news.body: RJ Harvey (hamstring) was upgraded to a full participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: RJ Harvey (hamstring) upgraded to full participant Thursday
news.impact: Harvey missed last week's game due to a hamstring injury that he has been dealing with, but he was able to return to a full practice on Thursday, so it seems likely that he will suit up and play in Week 3. He will likely continue to share the backfield with J.K. Dobbins (hip), though it looks like rookie Jonah Coleman (ankle) will be out of his hair for at least a week.

news.body: RJ Harvey (hamstring) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: RJ Harvey (hamstring) listed as limited Wednesday
news.impact: Harvey was able to practice in a limited fashion on Wednesday after missing last week's game due to a hamstring injury. It looks like he's trending towards playing in Week 3 and could see more work than usual if Jonah Coleman (ankle) is ruled out ahead of the team's matchup against the Rams on Sunday night.

news.body: RJ Harvey (hamstring) was seen practicing for the Broncos on Wednesday.
news.head: RJ Harvey (hamstring) seen practicing Wednesday
news.impact: The young running back was sidelined last week due to a hamstring injury, but it looks like he will have a chance to make his return to the lineup in Week 3, as he is participating in practice in some capacity to start the week on Wednesday. His potential return this week would mean less work for rookie Jonah Coleman (hamstring) moving forward.

news.body: Saquon Barkley (stinger) is off of the injury report and cleared to play for the Philadelphia Eagles against the Chicago Bears Monday night according to Mike Garafolo.
news.head: Saquon Barkley (stinger) off injury report for Eagles
news.impact: Barkley is good to go after logging full practice sessions to end the week for head coach Nick Sirianni, boosting a Philadelphia rushing attack that will look to take advantage of a susceptible Bears defense Monday night.

news.body: Saquon Barkley practiced again on Friday.
news.head: Saquon Barkley (stinger) practices Friday
news.impact: Barkley remains on track to be good to go for Monday's game against the Bears.

news.body: Saquon Barkley (stinger) told reporters that his MRI went well and he expects to play on Monday night.
news.head: Saquon Barkley (stinger) expects to play Monday
news.impact: Barkley underwent an MRI after suffering a stinger in last week's win over the Titans, but the results were apparently good and he reportedly expects to play on Monday night against the Bears. Fantasy managers should still keep close tabs on his status throughout the rest of the week to ensure that will be the case.

news.body: Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni did not have an update on the status of Saquon Barkley on Thursday.
news.head: Saquon Barkley (stinger) without update per HC Nick Sirianni
news.impact: The Eagles injury report will be released later in the afternoon. Tank Bigsby is worth stashing for now for fantasy managers just in case with Barkley.

news.body: Tony Pollard (ankle) will play in Sunday's game against the New York Giants.
news.head: Tony Pollard (ankle) will play Sunday
news.impact: Pollard spent all week on the team's injury report due to an ankle issue that he has been working through, but he is over it now and carries no injury designation ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Giants. He will see a very large workload if Tyjae Spears (ankle) is unable to play in Week 3 for the Titans.

news.body: Tony Pollard (ankle) will log a full practice session for the Tennessee Titans Friday according to Turron Davenport.
news.head: Tony Pollard (ankle) practicing fully Friday
news.impact: Pollard has increased his practice participation throughout the week, boding well for his chances of suiting up for head coach Robert Saleh against the New York Giants Sunday.

news.body: Tony Pollard (ankle) was upgraded to a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Tony Pollard (ankle) upgraded to limited Thursday
news.impact: Pollard was able to return to practice on Thursday after being sidelined due to an ankle injury on Wednesday. It looks like he's going to play this week, and if that's the case, he will see more work than usual in the event that Tyjae Spears (ankle) is unable to suit up against the Giants.

news.body: Tony Pollard (ankle) returned to practice for the Titans on Thursday.
news.head: Tony Pollard (ankle) returns to practice Thursday
news.impact: Pollard was seen participating in the open portion of Tennessee's practice on Thursday. That's a step in the right direction for his availability for Week 3, and he could be the team's clear-cut workhorse this week if Tyjae Spears (ankle) has to miss time.

news.body: Travis Etienne Jr. exited Sunday’s contest between the New Orleans Saints against the Las Vegas Raiders according to Ross Jackson.
news.head: Travis Etienne Jr. exits early Sunday
news.impact: Etienne Jr. headed to the locker room for further evaluation, rushing 13 times for 57 yards while also hauling in both of his targets for 13 yards prior to exiting. Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller will take over backfield duties in the running back’s absence.

news.body: Travis Etienne Jr. has been cleared for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
news.head: Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) good to go for Sunday
news.impact: Etienne has been dealing with a hamstring injury this week. He'll be a risky RB2 play for fantasy managers.

news.body: Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) was officially limited at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) officially limited Thursday
news.impact: Etienne was a limited participant for a second-straight practice on Thursday. He's still being affected by his hamstring injury, and it remains to be seen if it will affect his availability for Sunday's matchup against the Raiders or not. If it does, expect more work for Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller (illness) in that matchup.

news.body: Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) limited at practice Wednesday
news.impact: Etienne is a new addition to New Orleans' injury report, being listed with a hamstring injury that left him limited at practice on Wednesday. It remains unclear whether or not it will affect his availability for Week 3, and this is a situation fantasy managers should continue to monitor throughout the week, especially with Etienne losing so much work to Alvin Kamara in his return game last week.

news.body: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson tallied 76 rushing yards and a touchdown on 16 carries in the Patriots' 20-3 win over the Steelers.
news.head: TreVeyon Henderson finds the end zone in season debut
news.impact: Henderson missed Week 1 with an ankle injury, but made an immediate impact with a 39-yard touchdown early in the win over Pittsburgh. Rhamondre Stevenson lost a fumble and saw the bulk of the work go to Henderson after the turnover. Fantasy managers should expect both Stevenson and Henderson to have roles against the Jaguars in Week 3.

news.body: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is off of the injury report and officially good to go for Sunday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
news.head: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) officially good to go for Sunday
news.impact: New England's offense is set to get a much-needed boost this week with their young running back off of the injury report and set to make his season debut on Sunday. Henderson projects to be something of a 'boom-or-bust' fantasy option on a week-to-week basis while he continues to split work with Rhamondre Stevenson in the Patriots' backfield.

news.body: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) has been practicing in full this week and will be ready for Sunday's game.
news.head: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) ready for season debut
news.impact: Henderson was unable to go in Week 1, leaving the bulk of the backfield load to veteran Rhamondre Stevenson. Henderson is in his second NFL season after totaling over 1,100 yards of offense and 10 touchdowns across 17 regular-season games as a rookie.

news.body: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) logged a full practice session on Thursday.
news.head: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) logs full practice Thursday
news.impact: Henderson was able to log a second-straight full practice session on Thursday. He seems almost certain to play without any real limitations this week, as he also told reporters that he is ready to go for Sunday's game. His return to the lineup will mean less work for Rhamondre Stenson moving forward, but they could both be worthwhile starters on any given week.

news.body: Titans RB Tyjae Spears (ankle) is officially active for a Week 3 matchup with the Giants.
news.head: Tyjae Spears (ankle) officially active for Week 3
news.impact: Spears was listed as questionable to play Sunday, but was able to return and practice Friday. He should be expected to split time with Tony Pollard against the Giants.

news.body: Tyjae Spears (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the New York Giants.
news.head: Tyjae Spears (ankle) questionable for Sunday
news.impact: Spears was able to return to practice on Friday, but he is still not fully over his ankle injury and is officially questionable to play in Sunday's game. If he is ruled out, Tony Pollard will be primed for a large workload in a favorable matchup against the Giants this week.

news.body: Tyjae Spears (ankle) is returning to practice for the Tennessee Titans Friday according to Turron Davenport.
news.head: Tyjae Spears (ankle) practicing Friday
news.impact: Spears is back after being unable to practice Thursday, rejoining fellow backfield mate Tony Pollard (ankle) on the practice field for head coach Robert Saleh in preparation for a Week 3 matchup against the New York Giants.

news.body: Tyjae Spears (ankle) was officially a non-participant for the Titans on Thursday.
news.head: Tyjae Spears (ankle) officially a non-participant Thursday
news.impact: As expected, Spears was unable to practice again on Thursday because of the ankle injury that he's dealing with. Tony Pollard (ankle) was able to return to practice, however, so it looks like he will be primed for a big workload this week if the 25-year old is sidelined.

news.body: Tyler Allgeier ran for -1 yard on two carries in the Cardinals 36-30 loss against the 49ers on Sunday. He also caught 4-of-4 targets for 10 yards receiving.
news.head: Tyler Allgeier has quiet day Sunday
news.impact: Allgeier took a step back to rookie RB Jeremiyah Love for the first time this season on the day. If this trend continues, he'll remain a pure stash for fantasy managers.

news.body: Tyler Allgeier ran five times for 10 yards and caught both of his targets for 9 yards in the Cardinals' 31-7 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
news.head: Tyler Allgeier gets seven touches in loss
news.impact: Allgeier played second fiddle to Jeremiyah Love on Sunday, which is to be expected. He wasn't particularly efficient on his limited work, but no one in the offense really got going anyway. It was tough sledding for the veteran, but hopefully things will get a little easier against San Fransisco next Sunday.

news.body: Tyler Allgeier gained 61 yards on 17 carries and nine yards on two receptions in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.head: Tyler Allgeier leads Arizona rushing attack in Week 1
news.impact: Allgeier shouldered the majority of the backfield load for the Cardinals on Sunday, getting six more carries than Jeremiyah Love. Allgeier was not especially impressive, averaging just 3.6 yards per carry with a long of 11. Allgeier will remain involved, but the share of the carries should tilt more toward Love as the rookie gets further removed from the ankle sprain he sustained a month ago.

news.body: Tyler Allgeier was listed as the starting running back on the Cardinals' Week 1 depth chart.
news.head: Tyler Allgeier listed as starter on Cardinals depth chart
news.impact: Allgeier was listed as the starter ahead of rookie Jeremiyah Love after a training camp battle. Love has also been making his way back from an ankle sprain, which could be why Allgeier sees more carries in the early part of the season. If he does indeed get the start on Sunday, Allgeier could be an RB3 or deeper flex option in fantasy.

news.body: Woody Marks rushed for 15 yards and a touchdown on five carries in a 19-17 loss to the Colts. He caught his lone target for six yards.
news.head: Woody Marks finds the end zone in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Marks found the end zone for the first time this season on a one-yard plunge in the fourth quarter. With David Montgomery struggling over the last two weeks, the Texans may look to Marks to carry the ball more in Week 4 against Dallas.

news.body: Woody Marks ran for eight yards on eight carries in the Texans 20-6 loss against the Bengals on Sunday. He also caught 5-of-6 targets for 27 yards receiving.
news.head: Woody Marks active in receiving game Sunday
news.impact: Marks and David Montgomery were both completely shut down on the ground. Marks salvaged his afternoon with five receptions. He will be on the flex radar in deeper leagues next week against the Colts.

news.body: Woody Marks rushed for 42 yards on nine carries and caught his only target for a two-yard loss in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.head: Woody Marks gets 10 touches in Week 1
news.impact: Marks was certainly involved in the offense behind new workhorse back David Montgomery on Sunday. Marks averaged close to 5.0 yards per carry on his nine attempts. He'll remain a useful handcuff to Montgomery for now.

news.body: Texans coach Demeco Ryans said he is seeing a “year two jump” from Woody Marks.
news.head: Woody Marks: Texans HC DeMeco Ryans seeing year two jump
news.impact: Ryans noted specifically that Marks is looking faster and making better decisions compared to his rookie season. The Texans traded for David Montgomery who is expected to lead the backfield, but Marks should play a role behind him.

news.body: AJ Barner caught his only target for eight yards and ran in a one-yard touchdown on his only carry in Seattle's 31-7 win over Arizona.
news.head: AJ Barner runs in touchdown in win over Cardinals
news.impact: Barner's fantasy day was saved by the touchdown, as he hasn't gotten much volume to start the season. He's touchdown-or-bust right now and is best left on the bench or on waivers.

news.body: AJ Barner caught two passes for 13 yards in Wednesday's 13-10 win over the New England Patriots.
news.head: AJ Barner catches two passes Wednesday
news.impact: The Seahawks were able to pick up a win over the Patriots on Wednesday, but they didn't need to get Barner very involved in order to do so. He finished the game with just two catches for 13 yards, and there's not much reason to believe that he will bounce back and become a quality week-to-week option anytime soon.

news.body: AJ Barner is off the injury report for Wednesday’s game against the Patriots.
news.head: AJ Barner (oblique) off injury report Wednesday
news.impact: Barner practiced all week in full. He'll be a TE2 for fantasy managers going into the season.

news.body: AJ Barner was a full participant in practice on Monday.
news.head: AJ Barner (oblique) logs full practice Monday
news.impact: Barner remains on track to be a full-go for Wednesday’s season opener against the Patriots.

news.body: Brenton Strange caught both of his targets for 17 yards in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
news.head: Brenton Strange catches two balls in Week 2
news.impact: Strange was quiet in a game where the defenses led the way. The veteran tight end has now caught four of his five targets for 40 yards and a touchdown over two games. He will be on the TE2 radar in fantasy for his Week 3 matchup against the Patriots.

news.body: Brenton Strange caught two of three targets for 23 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday.
news.head: Brenton Strange grabs touchdown in win over Browns
news.impact: Strange was among ten other targeted receivers who were trying to feast off of an extremely small pie of 21 total targets. And he was one of the lucky ones with a touchdown. He should continue to see work as the top tight end for the offense, but things are so spread out that it might be hard to rely on him on a weekly basis.

news.body: The Jaguars signed Brenton Strange to a three-year contract extension.
news.head: Brenton Strange signs three-year extension with Jaguars
news.impact: The deal is worth “up to” $48 million with $25 million guaranteed. Strange missed five games last season, but emerged as a top threat in the passing game when he was healthy for Trevor Lawrence last season. Strange profiles as a borderline TE1 for fantasy managers with Nate Boerkircher and Tanner Koziol competing for snaps behind him.

news.body: Brenton Strange could the the Jags ‘“most important player” aside from Trevor Lawrence, according to Jags beat John Shipley. Shipley notes than despite missing five games last year, Strange still finished third in routes run.
news.head: Brenton Strange could be offense’s most important player’ behind Lawrence
news.impact: Strange is far and away the Jags TE1, and it doesn’t seem anyone is taking that job away from him. Tanner Koziol is next up as a pass catcher, but the rookie out of Houston is the TE3 at the moment and unlikely to impact Strange’s workload.

news.body: Brock Bowers caught 10-of-13 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders 35-27 win over the Saints.
news.head: Brock Bowers dominates in return Sunday
news.impact: Bowers was making his season debut and he did not miss a beat. He was involved early and often. He remains a high-end TE1 moving forward.

news.body: Brock Bowers (knee) is officially active for Week 3 for the Las Vegas Raiders against the New Orleans Saints.
news.head: Brock Bowers (knee) active for Week 3
news.impact: Bowers will take the field for his regular season debut after passing through pregame testing on his knee without any setbacks, providing quarterback Kirk Cousins with a dynamic pass-catching option against the Saints Sunday.

news.body: Brock Bowers (knee) is expected to play on Sunday against the Saints barring a surprise setback.
news.head: Brock Bowers (knee) expected to play on Sunday
news.impact: Bowers has been out for the first two weeks of the season after undergoing a meniscus trim surgery, but it looks like he will be back for Sunday. Start him in all formats, but temper expectations as he could start off a little slow.

news.body: Brock Bowers is listed as questionable for Sunday’s game against the Saints.
news.head: Brock Bowers (knee) listed questionable Sunday
news.impact: Bowers did not practice on Friday, but head coach Klint Kubiak said it was a planned day off. Bowers will need to be monitored closer to kickoff on Sunday.

news.body: Cade Otton caught 3-of-6 targets for 56 yards in the Buccaneers 23-16 loss against the Vikings on Sunday.
news.head: Cade Otton a safety blanket for the Buccaneers Sunday
news.impact: Otton was second on the team in targets on the day. He has seen at least five targets in all three weeks to start the season. He'll remain a high floor tight end play next week against the Packers.

news.body: Cade Otton caught 5-of-6 targets for 38 yards in the Buccaneers 23-19 loss against the Browns.
news.head: Cade Otton catches five passes Sunday
news.impact: Otton was a safety blanket all afternoon for Baker Mayfield. He remains a TE2 for fantasy managers.

news.body: Cade Otton caught 3-for-5 targets for 26 yards in the Buccaneers 33-27 loss against the Bengals on Sunday.
news.head: Cade Otton quiet Sunday
news.impact: Otton was third on the team in targets, but he was unable to turn it into much production. He remains a TE2 for fantasy managers.

news.body: The Bucs are re-signing TE Cade Otton.
news.head: Cade Otton re-signs with Bucs
news.impact: Otton was set to hit free agency, but he will be remaining with Tampa Bay and Baker Mayfield as a safety blanket. He should remain on the TE1/TE2 radar for fantasy managers.

news.body: Colston Loveland caught one of his three targets for three yards in the Bears' 9-3 Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
news.head: Colston Loveland catches one pass in Week 2
news.impact: Loveland has struggled to make an impact to begin the season, recording one reception or less in each of the first two games. The tight end remains a risky pass-catching option ahead of a Week 3 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.

news.body: Colston Loveland failed to catch either of his two targets in the Bears' 59-37 Week 1 win over the Carolina Panthers.
news.head: Colston Loveland sees two targets in Week 1
news.impact: Loveland was non-existent in an explosive Chicago offense for head coach Ben Johnson in the season opener, operating as more of an afterthought in the win. The tight end will look to get back on track in a Week 2 divisional contest against the Minnesota Vikings.

news.body: Colston Loveland caught a team-high 10 passes, on 13 targets, for 91 yards and a score in the Bears' 19-16 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
news.head: Colston Loveland catches 10 passes and scores TD in Week 18
news.impact: Loveland, the first-round pick out of Michigan, is starting to get hot at the right time for the Bears. Over the last two weeks, the tight end has caught 16 passes for 185 yards and two touchdowns. After a slow start to the season (11 catches in the first six weeks), Loveland has caught 47 passes over his last ten games. He will look to remain a focal point of the offense during the postseason.

news.body: Colston Loveland hauled in six of his team-leading 10 targets for 94 yards and one touchdown in the Bears' 42-38 Week 17 loss to the 49ers.
news.head: Colston Loveland sees 10 targets in Week 17 loss to 49ers
news.impact: Loveland has made the most of modest involvement in the Chicago passing attack of late, recording one touchdown in three of his last six games. The tight end remains a boom-or-bust tight end option in all formats for fantasy managers ahead of a Week 18 matchup against the Detroit Lions.

news.body: Dallas Goedert (knee) will not be placed on injured reserve but is still expected to be sidelined for a few weeks.
news.head: Dallas Goedert (knee) to avoid IR, expected to miss a few weeks
news.impact: Goedert suffered a knee injury last week and the team considered placing him on injured reserve, but they are not going to do so, as he is only expected to miss a few weeks while he recovers. This is good news for fantasy managers of the veteran, but they will still need to find a substitute for him for the foreseeable future while he's out. Zach Ertz will step up and see more work for the Eagles in his absence.

news.body: Dallas Goedert suffered a sprained MCL in Sunday’s win over the Titans.
news.head: Dallas Goedert suffers MCL sprain, to miss a few weeks
news.impact: The injury is expected to sideline Goedert for at least a few weeks. DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon should all step up even more in the passing game for Jalen Hurts.

news.body: Dallas Goedert caught one of his two targets for four yards in a 24-20 win over the Titans in Week 2.
news.head: Dallas Goedert held to one catch before knee injury
news.impact: Goedert left the game with a knee injury and did not return. Look for the team to update his status heading into a Week 3 matchup against the Bears. The Eagles are all of a sudden very thin at tight end with Eli Stowers and Grant Calcaterra both on injured reserve already.

news.body: Eagles TE Dallas Goedert (ankle) is officially listed as questionable to return Sunday.
news.head: Dallas Goedert (ankle) questionable to return
news.impact: Goedert appeared to have suffered the injury blocking in the second quarter. Johnny Mundt will see an increase in snaps with Goedert sidelined.

news.body: Dalton Kincaid hauled in two of his three targets for 38 yards and one fumble lost in the Bills' 24-16 Week 3 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: Dalton Kincaid quiet in Week 3 win over Chargers
news.impact: Kincaid was held in check by the Los Angeles defense, failing to surpass 90 receiving yards for the first time in three contests in the win. The tight end remains one of the more impactful pass-catching options for quarterback Josh Allen, with a Week 4 divisional matchup against the New England Patriots up next.

news.body: Dalton Kincaid caught 7-of-8 passing attempts for 95 yards and a touchdown in Thursday night's 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions.
news.head: Dalton Kincaid electric in win Thursday
news.impact: Kincaid's great start to the season continued on Thursday night. He was Buffalo's leading receiver against the Lions and was able to get into the end zone on one of his seven catches, which left him with a great fantasy total. It looks like he may be in the midst of a big breakout season right now, so long as he and QB Josh Allen stay healthy for the majority of the season.

news.body: Dalton Kincaid caught five of six targets for 130 yards in the Bills’ 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday.
news.head: Dalton Kincaid has breakout game against Texans
news.impact: Kincaid had arguably his best game as a pro, acheiving a career-high 130 receiving yards in what should have been tough sledding against Houston. He tied with Khalil Shakir for second in targets on the Bills, but vastly outproduced Shakir in yards. His downfield usage was encouraging, and it’s a promising start to his fourth season. Now to see if it keeps up.

news.body: The Buffalo Bills have exercised the fifth-year option on TE Dalton Kincaid.
news.head: Dalton Kincaid gets fifth-year option picked up
news.impact: Kincaid, a former first-round pick, is coming off his most efficient NFL season. The 26-year-old tight end hauled in 39 receptions for 571 receiving yards and 5 touchdowns. His contract is now guaranteed through 2027 as he continues to operate as one of Josh Allen’s top pass-catching options.

news.body: Dalton Schultz caught all three of his targets for 30 yards in a 19-17 loss to the Colts.
news.head: Dalton Schultz hauls in three catches in Week 3
news.impact: Schultz saw his lowest target share of the season Sunday and had an incredible drop of from his 12 receptions in Week 2. The Houston offense struggled in general against the Colts' defense, and they will need to bounce back against Dallas to avoid going 0-4 on the season.

news.body: Dalton Schultz returned to practice on Thursday.
news.head: Dalton Schultz (rest) back at practice Thursday
news.impact: After a huge performance on Sunday, Schultz received a rest day to begin the practice week. If Nico Collins remains sidelined, he'll be in line for TE1 volume once again.

news.body: Dalton Schultz (rest) missed Houston's practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Dalton Schultz (rest) misses practice Wednesday
news.impact: The Texans gave Schultz Wednesday's practice off as a veteran rest day for him after he caught 12 passes in Week 2. He should be back in the lineup very soon and will be primed for more work than usual again this week if Nico Collins (hamstring) is sidelined for another game.

news.body: Dalton Schultz caught 12-of-14 targets for 140 yards in the Texans 20-6 loss against the Bengals on Sunday.
news.head: Dalton Schultz explodes for 12 catches Sunday
news.impact: Schultz was the Texans pass catcher who stepped up big time in the absence of Nico Collins. He'll remain a strong TE1 play if Collins remains sidelined next week.

news.body: Darren Waller (rest) returned to practice and was a full participant on Thursday.
news.head: Darren Waller (rest) returns to practice Thursday
news.impact: As expected, the veteran was back at practice on Thursday after getting the day off on Wednesday as a veteran rest day. He should be a full go for Week 3 and will continue to have touchdown upside on a week-to-week basis moving forward.

news.body: Darren Waller (rest) was a non-participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Darren Waller (rest) a non-participant Wednesday
news.impact: To no surprise, Carolina gave Waller the day off on Wednesday as a veteran rest day. He should be back at practice on Thursday and is expected to be a full go for Week 3 at this point.

news.body: Darren Waller caught all three of his targets for 33 yards and two scores in the Panthers' 34-3 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
news.head: Darren Waller snags two touchdown passes in win
news.impact: Waller had himself a great fantasy day, heavily boosted by the two touchdowns. He's only had five targets so far this year, but if the Panthers are willing to use him in the red zone, he's worth a look for those needing a tight end streamer.

news.body: Darren Waller (rest) returned to practice as a full participant on Thursday.
news.head: Darren Waller (rest) returns to practice Thursday
news.impact: As expected, the veteran tight end was back and practicing at full capacity for the Panthers on Thursday. He should play in Week 2 but shouldn't be considered a reliable fantasy option at this point in the season.

news.body: George Kittle caught 6-of-7 targets for 82 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
news.head: George Kittle scores twice Sunday
news.impact: Kittle took on a bigger role with Mike Evans (rib) exiting early. He hauled in two touchdowns from Brock Purdy in the win. He remains a strong TE1, especially if Evans misses time.

news.body: George Kittle secured all four of his targets for 80 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
news.head: George Kittle finds the end zone in Week 2
news.impact: With his Achilles injury further behind him, Kittle's playmaking ability was on display Sunday. The veteran TE led the 49ers in receiving yards and had the longest gain of the day with a 40-yard pickup. Kittle also scored his first touchdown of the campaign on a 12-yard pass from Brock Purdy early in the third quarter. As long as he's healthy, Kittle is among the top TEs in the league.

news.body: George Kittle (Achilles) will be good to go for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: George Kittle (Achilles) good to go for Sunday
news.impact: As expected, Kittle carries no injury designation heading into the weekend and will be available to play against the Dolphins. It seems likely that he will continue to be limited in some capacity, though it looks like the 49ers are planning on ramping his workload up more and more each week moving forward.

news.body: George Kittle (Achilles) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
news.head: George Kittle (Achilles) limited again Thursday
news.impact: Kittle was limited for another practice on Thursday, which should come as no surprise given that the team is trying to be cautious while he ramps his workload back up after suffering a devastating Achilles injury at the end of last season. He should return to a full workload sometime within the next few weeks if his recovery continues to progress well, at which point he will likely return to being a great fantasy asset for the remainder of the season.

news.body: Harold Fannin Jr. caught 5-of-6 targets for 54 yards in the Browns 23-19 win over the Buccaneers.
news.head: Harold Fannin Jr. catches five passes Sunday
news.impact: Fannin was able to bounce back after being held without a catch last week. He remains a low-end TE1 heading into next week against the Panthers.

news.body: Harold Fannin Jr. caught two of three targets for 21 yards in the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
news.head: Harold Fannin Jr. held in check on Sunday
news.impact: Fannin was held in check on Sunday, along with the rest of the Browns' offense. He will hope for better days next week against the Buccaneers.

news.body: Harold Fannin Jr. missed practice on Friday for personal reasons.
news.head: Harold Fannin Jr. (personal) does not practice Friday
news.impact: It is not an injury related absence for Fannin. He'll likely be back at practice soon.

news.body: Harold Fannin Jr. (groin) has been cleared to participate in the Browns training camp after undergoing offseason surgery.
news.head: Harold Fannin Jr. cleared for training camp activities
news.impact: It turns out Fannin was cleared two weeks ago, it’s just seemingly been kept under wraps. There is much to be decided among the Browns receivers pecking order sharing the field with him, but he should be a favorite to be the Browns top target in the passing game, ala Brock Bowers or Trey McBride-lite.

news.body: Patriots TE Hunter Henry caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Patriots' 20-3 win over the Steelers.
news.head: Hunter Henry hauls in three passes in Week 2 win
news.impact: Henry led the team in targets and was tied with Romeo Doubs for the team lead in receptions. Henry should continue to see a steady volume with A.J. Brown on injured reserve. The veteran tight end will head to Jacksonville for a Week 3 matchup with the Jaguars.

news.body: Hunter Henry caught three passes for 26 yards in Wednesday's 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
news.head: Hunter Henry hauls in three passes Wednesday
news.impact: New England's offense wasn't very effective on Wednesday night, and Henry was no exception to that. He totaled just 26 scoreless yards against the Seahawks, which left him with a poor fantasy total. His value as a streaming option may be diminished this year with Eli Raridon seemingly primed to be more involved at the tight end position for the Patriots.

news.body: Hunter Henry has agreed to a two year extension with the New England Patriots. He had one year left remaining on his contract, but is now locked in till the end of 2028.
news.head: Hunter Henry agrees to two year extension with Patriots
news.impact: It’s great news for Henry managers, but bad news for Eli Raridon truthers. The rookie and promising young tight end could still break out as Henry ages out, but this certainly puts a damper on his prospects in the short term. But getting back to Henry, he should be a solid target later in fantasy drafts this year.

news.body: Hunter Henry is listed as questionable for the Super Bowl next Sunday against the Seahawks.
news.head: Hunter Henry (rest) listed as questionable for Super Bowl
news.impact: Henry closed the week with a full practice on Friday. He should be good to go heading into next week.

news.body: Isaiah Likely hauled in 5-of-10 targets for 33 yards in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: Isaiah Likely hauls in five passes Monday
news.impact: Likely didn't put up great numbers on Monday night, finishing with just 33 yards in a loss to the Rams. He was still the most targeted player on the team by far, however, which is a good sign that he will bounce back and return to form sometime in the near future. His bounce back may be delayed is Jaxson Dart (knee) has to miss time for the Giants.

news.body: Isaiah Likely caught eight passes for 78 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
news.head: Isaiah Likely hauls in two touchdowns in win Sunday
news.impact: Likely exceeded expectations in his first game as a Giant on Sunday. He led the team in receptions, receiving yards, and touchdowns on the night, scoring twice in what turned out to be a huge win over the Cowboys. His involvement on this offense looks great right now and he will likely be one of the hot waiver additions this week in any league he's not already rostered in.

news.body: The Giants are signing Isaiah Likely to a three-year, $40 million contract.
news.head: Isaiah Likely signs three-year deal with Giants
news.impact: The deal is worth to $47.5 million as Likely reunites with John Harbaugh. He should take on a bigger role with the Giants than what he had in Baltimore. He will be on the TE1 radar for fantasy managers.

news.body: The Giants are expected to show interest in free agent TE Isaiah Likely.
news.head: Isaiah Likely to draw interest from Giants
news.impact: Likely has history with new Giants head coach John Harbaugh. New York will be looking to bring in more offensive weapons to help the development of Jaxson Dart as they're likely losing Wan'Dale Robinson in free agency. Likely is one of the top tight ends available in free agency.

news.body: Jake Ferguson caught all four of his targets for 43 yards and two touchdowns in the Cowboys win over the Commanders.
news.head: Jake Ferguson finds the end zone twice in Week 2
news.impact: Ferguson was quiet in Week 1, so this was a much needed bounce back performance. The 27-year-old remains the primary pass catching option out of the tight end group. Ferguson will look to build on this performance in Week 3 against the Ravens.

news.body: Jake Ferguson caught just two passes for six yards in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the New York Giants.
news.head: Jake Ferguson quiet in loss Sunday
news.impact: The veteran tight end didn't make an impact on Sunday night. He was held to just two catches and six total yards against the Giants, which was a symptom of Dallas' offensive struggles against their divisional rivals. Ferguson isn't expected to be fantasy relevant anytime in the foreseeable future.

news.body: The Cowboys restructured TE Jake Ferguson’s contract.
news.head: Jake Ferguson restructures contract with Cowboys
news.impact: Ferguson’s $7.25 million base salary was turned into a signing bonus. The Cowboys now have $33.2 million in salary cap space.

news.body: Jake Ferguson missed practice on Saturday due to personal reasons.
news.head: Jake Ferguson (personal) misses practice Saturday
news.impact: Ferguson was away from the team on Saturday.

news.body: Juwan Johnson caught 4-of-4 passes for 66 yards in the Saints 24-17 win over the Ravens.
news.head: Juwan Johnson hauls in four passes in Week 2
news.impact: Johnson continues to serve as the primary passing option out of the Saints' tight end group. The 30-year-old veteran has topped 50+ receiving yards in the first two games of the season and appears poised to turn in solid performances in an improved Saints' offense. Johnson and the Saints will take on the Raiders in Week 3.

news.body: Juwan Johnson is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
news.head: Juwan Johnson (illness) off injury report Week 2
news.impact: Johnson was a late addition to the injury report this week with an illness. He'll be on the TE1/TE2 radar for fantasy managers this week.

news.body: Juwan Johnson (illness) returned to practice as a limited participant on Thursday.
news.head: Juwan Johnson (illness) returns to practice Thursday
news.impact: Johnson was back at practice on Thursday after being absent from practice on Wednesday due to an illness of some kind. He should be fully good to go for Sunday's game against the Ravens, and fantasy managers should continue to view him as a viable starter for the foreseeable future, especially with Chris Olave (hamstring) now popping up on the injury report and at risk of missing a bit of time.

news.body: Juwan Johnson (illness) did not take part in New Orleans' practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Juwan Johnson (illness) doesn't practice Wednesday
news.impact: Johnson is a new addition to New Orleans' injury report, being listed with an illness of some kind that left him absent from practice on Wednesday. He's likely considered day-to-day at this point and seems to have a good chance to play in Week 2. If he's active he will be worth starting in a big matchup against the Ravens on Sunday.

news.body: Kenyon Sadiq caught 7-of-8 targets for 105 yards and a touchdown in a 31-24 loss to the Jets.
news.head: Kenyon Sadiq finds the end zone in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Sadiq caught his first NFL touchdown pass on a great catch in the second quarter as he stretched out to haul in the pass in the end zone. The rookie tight end was second on the team in receptions, yards, and targets, just behind Garrett Wilson. Sadiq and the Jets will take on the Bears on the road in Week 4.

news.body: Kenyon Sadiq caught two of his three targets for 17 yards in the Jets' 20-17 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 2.
news.head: Kenyon Sadiq catches two passes in Week 2
news.impact: Sadiq fell back to earth after an impactful Week 1 performance, finishing with less than three receptions in the losing effort. The tight end remains one of many unproven pass-catching options as part of a revamped Jets passing attack ahead of a Week 3 contest against the Detroit Lions.

news.body: Kenyon Sadiq caught all three of his targets for 21 yards and added a three-yard rushing touchdown in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 2.
news.head: Kenyon Sadiq rushes for TD in Week 1
news.impact: Sadiq turned in a quiet outing in the passing attack but he scored the Jets' first TD of the season on his three-yard carry in the first quarter. The team's willingness to use the first-round rookie in the running game is an encouraging development for his fantasy value moving forward. Sadiq will be a solid TE2 in Week 2 against the Packers.

news.body: Kenyon Sadiq (groin) is without an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans.
news.head: Kenyon Sadiq (groin) without injury designation for Sunday
news.impact: The rookie will be available to make his NFL debut on Sunday. He is fully over his groin injury at this point and should have no major limitations in this matchup against the Titans. Fantasy managers shouldn't have high expectations for him in this matchup, however.

news.body: Kyle Pitts Sr. caught just one of two targets for five yards in the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
news.head: Kyle Pitts Sr. snags single pass in win
news.impact: Pitts took a backseat to Drake London and Bijan Robinson in this game, with Michael Penix heavily favoring London in terms of target share. Pitts was productive last year both with London on and off the field, but Penix has been so fixated on London in his starts that it's tough to trust Pitts. He is a bit of a shaky fantasy start until his workload improves.

news.body: Kyle Pitts Sr. caught one of three targets for 15 yards in the Falcons' 34-3 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
news.head: Kyle Pitts Sr. snags one pass in win
news.impact: With the Falcons' QB play being so abysmal, it's hard to take anything away from the last two weeks. Hopefully we will see Michael Penix on Thursday to help bring some clarity and stability to the passing game.

news.body: Kyle Pitts Sr. failed to catch his lone target in a 20-13 loss to the Steelers in Week 1.
news.head: Kyle Pitts Sr. held without a catch in Week 1
news.impact: It was a rough day for the Atlanta passing attack as third-string QB Cooper Rush only passed for 143 yards. Pitts will hope to bounce back in Week 2 against the Panthers, although he will be tough to trust in fantasy as long as Rush is under center.

news.body: Kyle Pitts Sr. has agreed to a 3-year, $54 million extension with the Atlanta Falcons.
news.head: Kyle Pitts Sr. agrees to 3-year, $54 million extension with Falcons
news.impact: After coming off arguably his best season as a pro, Pitts gets the bag. He will operate as the teams second target behind Drake London and TE1 in a tight end friendly Stefanski system. It’s wheels up for the still young Pitts.

news.body: Mark Andrews caught 6-of-7 targets for 49 yards in the Ravens 24-17 loss to the Saints.
news.head: Mark Andrews hauls in six passes in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Andrews ranked second on the team in targets, receptions, and yardage in the loss Sunday. With Zay Flowers (hamstring) out, Andrews should continue to see an increase in targets behind Rashod Bateman. Andrews and the Ravens will take on the Cowboys in Week 3.

news.body: Mark Andrews hauled in four of his six targets for 49 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.head: Mark Andrews sees six targets in Week 1 win
news.impact: Andrews received sizeable volume in the Baltimore passing attack, finishing tied for first in targets in the win. The veteran tight end remains a reliable option ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.

news.body: Mark Andrews caught two of his three targets for 14 yards in a 26-24 loss to the Steelers in Week 18.
news.head: Mark Andrews catches two passes in Week 18
news.impact: Andrews was quiet as the Ravens lost the AFC North and will miss the playoffs. The veteran tight end wraps up his 2025 season with 48 catches for 422 yards and five touchdowns while appearing in all 17 of the Ravens' games. Andrews' days as an elite tight end appear to be over as the team did not prioritize getting him the ball in 2025.

news.body: Mark Andrews caught all four of his targets for 28 yards in the Ravens' 41-24 win over the Packers.
news.head: Mark Andrews snags four passes in win
news.impact: You would think Andrews would have a better game given the number of points the Ravens put up, but it was almost all done on the ground. He's tough to trust for fantasy at this point.

news.body: Oronde Gadsden II failed to catch any of his three targets in the Chargers' 24-16 loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 3.
news.head: Oronde Gadsden II sees three targets in Week 3
news.impact: Gadsden II has been minimally involved in the Los Angeles passing attack early on, seeing three targets or less in each of the first three games. The tight end remains difficult to trust ahead of a Week 4 contest against the Seattle Seahawks.

news.body: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said TE Oronde Gadsden II is "ready to step up."
news.head: Oronde Gadsden II 'ready to step up' per HC Jim Harbaugh
news.impact: Gadsden will be stepping into a bigger role with both David Njoku and Charlie Kolar sidelined. He'll be a viable streamer for fantasy managers.

news.body: Oronde Gadsden II caught two passes for 18 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.head: Oronde Gadsden II hauls in touchdown Sunday
news.impact: Gadsden didn't see a lot of opportunities on Sunday, but he was able to capitalize on one of them by scoring Los Angeles' lone touchdown through the air against the Raiders. He still didn't have a great fantasy total, but he may see an increase in work moving forward with David Njoku (knee) possibly needing to miss time.

news.body: Oronde Gadsden II caught both of his targets for 32 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
news.head: Oronde Gadsden II hauls in two passes Sunday
news.impact: Gadsden was clearly the second option at TE behind newly acquired veteran David Njoku on Sunday. However, Gadsden did show off his big-play ability with a 26-yard gain in the second quarter. The hype was real around Gadsden for a time last season, but his fantasy value is capped with Njoku now firmly in the mix. Gadsden is a boom-or-bust option at the moment.

news.body: Pat Freiermuth caught 2-of-4 targets for 30 yards in a 30-27 win over the Bengals.
news.head: Pat Freiermuth hauls in two passes in Week 3
news.impact: Freiermuth has yet to find consistent success this season, and has seen his production dip each week since the season opener. The 27-year-old veteran will continue to compete with Darnell Washington for targets as the Steelers take on the Browns in Week 4.

news.body: Steelers TE Pat Freiermuth caught 4-of-5 targets for 32 yards and rushed once for two yards in the Steelers 20-3 loss to the Patriots.
news.head: Pat Freiermuth hauls in four passes in Week 2
news.impact: Freiermuth has logged five targets in both games this season and appears to have built a rapport with Aaron Rodgers. With Michael Pittman dealing with an ankle injury, the veteran tight end could be a solid option heading into a Week 3 matchup with the Bengals.

news.body: Pat Freiermuth caught all five of his targets for 46 yards and a touchdown in a 20-13 win over the Falcons in Week 1.
news.head: Pat Freiermuth finds the end zone in Week 1 win
news.impact: Freiermuth kicked off the season with a promising outing in the win over Atlanta. He hauled in Aaron Rodgers' lone touchdown pass on a six-yard catch in the second quarter while tying for second on the team in receptions. Freiermuth will settle in as a TE2 in fantasy heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Patriots.

news.body: Pat Freiermuth caught three of his five targets for 51 yards in a 26-24 win over the Ravens in Week 18.
news.head: Pat Freiermuth goes for 51 yards in Week 18
news.impact: Freiermuth finished third on the Steelers in receiving in the win. The veteran tight end wraps the regular season with 41 catches for 486 yards and four touchdowns while appearing in all 17 of the Steelers' games. He will now prepare to take on the Texans at home in the Wild-Card round of the playoffs.

news.body: Sam LaPorta caught 3-of-4 targets for 44 yards in a 31-24 win over the Jets.
news.head: Sam LaPorta tallies three receptions in Week 3
news.impact: LaPorta saw the bulk of the targets go to Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs in the win over the Jets. Fantasy managers will hope that LaPorta can become more involved against the Panthers in Week 4.

news.body: Sam LaPorta hauled in 6-of-7 targets for 52 yards and a touchdown in Thursday night's 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Sam LaPorta hauls in touchdown Thursday
news.impact: LaPorta had a good showing on Thursday night. He caught all but one of his targets and turned that into 52 yards and a touchdown in a shootout loss against the Buffalo Bills. He might struggle with consistency moving forward but will continue to have as high of a TD upside as anyone for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Sam LaPorta caught five of his eight targets for 48 yards in the Lions' 31-30 Week 1 win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.head: Sam LaPorta catches five passes in Week 1 win
news.impact: LaPorta saw sizeable volume in his return to the lineup for head coach Dan Campbell, joining explosive wideouts Jameson Williams and Amon-Ra St. Brown in finishing with eight or more targets in the win. The tight end remains a stable option in all formats as a primary pass-catching option in the Detroit offense ahead of a Week 2 contest against the Buffalo Bills.

news.body: Sam LaPorta (hip) is off of the injury report ahead of Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.
news.head: Sam LaPorta (hip) off injury report for Sunday
news.impact: LaPorta is now off of the injury report after dealing with a hip injury for the latter part of the preseason. He should be a full go for Week 1 and will remain a startable fantasy option in this matchup and beyond.

news.body: Terrance Ferguson (ankle) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Terrance Ferguson (ankle) good to go for Sunday
news.impact: As expected, Ferguson has been cleared to play for Week 3 after logging a full practice on both Thursday and Friday. He shouldn't have any limitations and is expected to be a viable fantasy option this week with Puka Nacua (hip) likely to be sidelined against the Broncos.

news.body: Terrance Ferguson (ankle) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Terrance Ferguson (ankle) listed as limited Wednesday
news.impact: Ferguson was estimated to be a limited participant at Wednesday's walk-through for the Rams. He's managing an ankle injury right now, but it doesn't seem to be more than a minor issue for him at this point. Fantasy managers should keep tabs on updates about his health and about the health of Puka Nacua (hip), as the young tight end benefited greatly when Los Angeles was missing their star wideout last week.

news.body: Terrance Ferguson caught 6-of-9 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
news.head: Terrance Ferguson plays well in win Monday
news.impact: Ferguson looked great on Monday night. He saw more work than usual with Puka Nacua (hip) out of the lineup for Los Angeles, and he was able to capitalize by putting up 54 yards and scoring a touchdown against the Giants. He has shown his talent and could continue to have week-to-week upside moving forward, although good games will be hard to predict when Nacua makes his return to the lineup.

news.body: Terrance Ferguson failed to catch his lone target in the Rams' 27-7 blowout loss to the 49ers.
news.head: Terrance Ferguson quiet in loss to 49ers
news.impact: The hopeful breakout for Ferguson came to a screeching halt on Thursday, with the tight end failing to garner a target until late in the game, and failing to bring it in at that. However, the entire Rams offense was dysfunctional; no one had a great day for fantasy aside from maybe Kyren Williams and Puka Nacua, depending on your criteria. And second, Ferguson was present on most of the snaps when the starters were in, a big increase from his part time role in 2025. Hopefully, with his snaps now increased, the targets will come. We may just have to wait a week for the Rams to figure out what happened to them and get back on track.

news.body: T.J. Hockenson caught 2-of-4 targets for 11 yards receiving in the Vikings 23-16 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
news.head: T.J. Hockenson quiet Sunday
news.impact: Hockenson was uninvolved despite Justin Jefferson (ankle) exiting early. He could be in the streaming conversation next week against the Dolphins if Jefferson is sidelined.

news.body: T.J. Hockenson caught three of his four targets for 29 yards in the Vikings' 9-3 Week 2 win over the Chicago Bears.
news.head: T.J. Hockenson catches three passes in Week 2 win
news.impact: Hockenson has made the most of modest involvement in the Minnesota passing attack to begin the season, recording three of more receptions in each of the first two games. The tight end remains one of the more risky pass-catching options for fantasy managers ahead of a Week 3 contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

news.body: T.J. Hockenson caught 4-of-5 targets for 36 yards in the Vikings 39-22 win over the Packers.
news.head: T.J. Hockenson hauls in touchdown Sunday
news.impact: Hockenson caught one of the three touchdowns thrown by Carson Wentz. He could be on the TE1 radar in a favorable matchup next week against the Bears.

news.body: The Vikings restructured the contract of TE T.J. Hockenson.
news.head: T.J. Hockenson restructures contract with Vikings
news.impact: Hockenson is coming off one of the worst seasons of his career. He'll now be two years removed from a knee injury he suffered in 2024. The move saves $5 million against the cap for the Vikings.

news.body: Travis Kelce hauled in both of his targets for 59 yards and one touchdown in the Chiefs' 24-10 Week 3 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Travis Kelce finds end zone in Week 3 win over Dolphins
news.impact: Kelce has been impactful to begin the season, recording over 55 receiving yards in each of the first three contests. The veteran tight end has turned back the clock as part of a revamped Chiefs offense for head coach Andy Reid, with a Week 4 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders up next.

news.body: Travis Kelce hauled in 9-of-11 targets for 101 yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.head: Travis Kelce dominant in overtime win Sunday
news.impact: Kelce looked great on Sunday night. He led the team in receptions and racked up 101 receiving yards on the night, a number which he failed to hit at all last season. His touchdown was the cherry on top for fantasy managers, and he will likely continue to have good week-to-week value if Patrick Mahomes and KC's offense continues to look this good moving forward.

news.body: Travis Kelce caught 3-of-5 targets for 71 yards in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Travis Kelce solid in win Monday
news.impact: Kelce wasn't very involved for much of Monday night's game, but he was able to haul in a big catch at one point that helped to leave him with a solid 71 yards on the night. Fantasy managers should be pleased with his performance in this matchup but should not expect him to be a TE1 on a week-to-week basis for the foreseeable future, especially with Kansas City seemingly wanting to operate as a run-heavy team this season.

news.body: The Chiefs re-signed TE Travis Kelce to a three-year, $54.735 million contract.
news.head: Travis Kelce officially re-signs with Chiefs on three-year deal
news.impact: Kelce was reported to have signed a one-year contract, but it is now a three-year deal. He caught 76 passes for 851 yards and five touchdowns last season, and will remain in Kansas City for three more seasons.

news.body: Trey McBride caught 9-of-11 targets for 75 yards in the Cardinals 36-30 loss against the Cardinals on Sunday.
news.head: Trey McBride hauls in nine passes Sunday
news.impact: McBride continues to be the safety blanket for Jacoby Brissett all over the field every week. He and Brock Bowers remain 1A and 1B among the tight end position.

news.body: Trey McBride caught eight of 10 targets for 41 yards and a score in the Cardinals' 31-7 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
news.head: Trey McBride snags touchdown in loss to Seattle
news.impact: McBride was the only thing working for the offense on Sunday, and even that only lasted but for so long. Seattle completely shut down the Cardinals in the second half, and McBride with them. But, it's doubtful any fantasy manager will complain about eight catches for 40+ yards and a score from their tight end.

news.body: Trey McBride (rest/back) did not take part in Arizona's practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Trey McBride (rest/back) doesn't practice Wednesday
news.impact: Arizona gave their star tight end the day off on Wednesday as a rest day. He was also listed with a back issue of some kind, but it seems to be nothing serious and isn't likely to play a factor on his availability for Week 2. He will remain a top-tier fantasy asset every time he's healthy and on the field for the Cardinals.

news.body: Trey McBride hauled in 9-of-13 targets for 95 yards and one touchdown in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.head: Trey McBride starts season with strong performance
news.impact: McBride is arguably the league's top fantasy asset at tight end, and he certainly looked the part in Week 1. Coming off back-to-back seasons with more than 100 receptions and 1,100 yards, McBride was QB Jacoby Brissett's favorite target on Sunday, getting five more looks than the next-closest Arizona pass catcher.

news.body: Tucker Kraft caught four of eight targets for 26 yards in the Packers' 35-14 loss to Atlanta on Thursday.
news.head: Tucker Kraft snags four passes in loss to Atlanta
news.impact: Kraft could have had a slightly bigger day had he held onto the football in what ended up being ruled a drop. The defensive back made a fantastic punch at the ball right as Kraft was corralling it into his chest, forcing a dropped pass. Kraft is still worth starting, and with that eight-target total, he has now beaten his season high in targets (previously six). The volume is there; the results just haven't quite followed yet.

news.body: Tucker Kraft caught two of his three targets for 15 yards in the Packers' 20-17 Week 2 win over the New York Jets.
news.head: Tucker Kraft quiet in Week 2 win
news.impact: Kraft was unable to make a significant impact as part of an underwhelming Green Bay passing attack, finishing with less than four receptions in each of the first two games. The tight end will look to get back on track for fantasy managers against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 3.

news.body: Tucker Kraft caught 3-of-6 targets for 65 yards in the Packers 39-22 loss against the Vikings.
news.head: Tucker Kraft totals 65 yards Sunday
news.impact: Kraft was playing in his first game back from his torn ACL. He was on a snap count in his first game back. He remains a TE1 heading into next week against the Jets.

news.body: Tucker Kraft has agreed to a four-year, $75 million deal with the Green Bay Packers. The deal is worth up to $92 million.
news.head: Tucker Kraft signs four year, $75 million deal with Packers
news.impact: Kraft was on his way to a massive season in 2025 before going down with a torn ACL. He gets his payday as the Packers lock in their emergeing star for the long haul.

news.body: Tyler Warren caught 9-of-10 targets for 55 yards in a 19-17 win over the Texans.
news.head: Tyler Warren hauls in nine passes in Week 3 win
news.impact: Warren set a new career high in receptions Sunday and continues to see plenty of opportunities in the Colts' offense this season. Fantasy managers should expect Warren to continue to see plenty of targets against Washington with Alec Pierce (heel) out.

news.body: Tyler Warren hauled in 6-of-7 targets for 21 yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.head: Tyler Warren hauls in touchdown Sunday
news.impact: The young tight end had an up-and-down night on Sunday. On one hand, he finished with a touchdown and six catches on the night, which led to good results in PPR leagues. On the other hand, he only totaled 21 yards on his seven targets, which is poor as far as efficiency goes. Fantasy managers should continue to expect high volume from him moving forward, especially with Alec Pierce (heel) seemingly set to miss some time.

news.body: Tyler Warren hauled in three of his five targets for 13 yards and one touchdown in a 41-23 Week 1 loss to the Baltimore Ravens.
news.head: Tyler Warren finds end zone in Week 1 loss
news.impact: Warren was mostly bottled up by a stiff Baltimore defense, averaging 4.3 yards per reception in the Week 1 loss. The tight end remains a primary pass-catching offense for head coach Shane Steichen ahead of a Week 2 contest against the Kansas City Chiefs.

news.body: Tyler Warren was able to practice on Tuesday.
news.head: Tyler Warren (groin) practices Tuesday
news.impact: Warren has been working his way back from a minor groin issue. He should be good to go for Week 1 next week.

news.body: A.J. Brown (ankle) is expected to miss at least six weeks for the New England Patriots according to Ian Rapoport.
news.head: A.J. Brown (ankle) out at least six weeks
news.impact: Brown was placed on injured reserve after suffering the ankle injury in New England’s Week 1 loss to the Seattle Seahawks Wednesday night, leaving head coach Mike Vrable without his top pass-catching option for the foreseeable future. In the wideout’s absence Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs, and DeMario Douglas will need to step up for quarterback Drake Maye early in the season.

news.body: A.J. Brown (ankle) has been placed on injured reserve by the New England Patriots according to Adam Schefter.
news.head: A.J. Brown (ankle) placed on injured reserve

news.body: A.J. Brown (ankle) is expected to miss at least four weeks with a high ankle sprain that he sustained early in the third quarter of the Patriots game against the Seahawks on Wednesday night.
news.head: A.J. Brown (ankle) expect to miss at least four weeks
news.impact: It’s a big blow to Brown’s Fantasy stock to start the season. In his absence, expect Hunter Henry and Romeo Doubs to see more work. However, with Doubs was struggling to find snaps and catch the ball, it’s possible that Demario Douglas could be a nice PPR sleeper.

news.body: A.J. Brown (ankle) is believed to have suffered a high ankle sprain in last nights game against the Seahawks. He will have an MRI today to determine the extent of the injury and how much time he will miss.
news.head: A.J. Brown (ankle) believed to have suffered high-ankle sprain on Wednesday
news.impact: It’s a tough start to Browns Patriot tenure. He went down early in the third quarter and did not return, leaving Drake Maye to lean on Hunter Henry, Demario Douglas, and Mack Hollins with fellow newcomer Romeo Doubs struggling to catch anything. Doubs should bounce back, and if Brown is out for any period of time, expect Doubs and Henry to have some more fantasy appeal, with Douglas as a PPR dart throw in deep formats.

news.body: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 4-of-8 targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in a 31-24 win over the Jets.
news.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown finds the end zone in Week 3 win
news.impact: St. Brown was not able to capitalize on his eight targets, but was able to help salvage the day with a touchdown in the second quarter. St. Brown now has five touchdowns through the first three games of the season and will look to build on a strong start to the season against the Panthers in Week 4.

news.body: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 6-of-8 targets for 142 yards and two touchdowns in Thursday night's 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown scores twice in loss Thursday
news.impact: St. Brown was on fire on Thursday night. He had a slow start, but he ended up finishing the game with a team high in receptions and receiving yards while finding the end zone twice against the Bills. He will continue to be a top-tier fantasy option moving forward, especially in PPR scoring formats.

news.body: Amon-Ra St. Brown hauled in 10 of his team-leading 14 targets for 67 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions' 31-30 Week 1 win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown hauls in 10 receptions in Week 1 win over Saints
news.impact: St. Brown was dynamic in the season-opening contest for head coach Dan Campbell, hauling in both of quarterback Jared Goff's touchdown passes in the win. The wideout remains an elite WR1 option in all formats ahead of a Week 2 road matchup against the Buffalo Bills.

news.body: The Lions restructured the contract of WR Amon-Ra St. Brown.
news.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown has contract restructured by Lions
news.impact: LT Penei Sewell also had his contract restructured. The Lions created $35.68 million in cap space.

news.body: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) is off of the injury report ahead of Week 3's matchup against the New England Patriots.
news.head: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) off injury report for Week 3
news.impact: Thomas is now off of the injury report and should be a full go heading into a Week 3 matchup against the New England Patriots. He isn't expected to be a strong fantasy option for the foreseeable future, however.

news.body: Brian Thomas Jr. caught three of his eight targets for 40 yards in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
news.head: Brian Thomas Jr. goes for 40 yards in Week 2
news.impact: Thomas seemed healthy after dealing with a shoulder injury in Week 1. He wound up finishing second on the Jags in all receiving categories while drawing an encouraging eight targets. Thomas is clearly behind Parker Washington in the pecking order, but he appears to be ahead of Jakobi Meyers, making him a solid WR3 in fantasy moving forward. He will face the Patriots in Week 3.

news.body: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) has been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) cleared to play Sunday
news.impact: Thomas suffered a shoulder injury during the team's season opener last week, but he was able to practice all week and won't miss any time because of it. He has been cleared to play on Sunday and should continue to contribute in his usual capacity for the Jaguars for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
news.head: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) limited again Thursday
news.impact: The young wideout remains banged up, still limited at practice due to a shoulder injury that he suffered in the season opener. It looks more likely than not that he will play in Week 2, but in the off-chance that he's sidelined, Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers will both benefit from his absence.

news.body: Carnell Tate caught three of his five targets for 27 yards in a 24-20 loss to the Eagles in Week 2.
news.head: Carnell Tate catches three passes in Week 2
news.impact: Tate finished fourth on the team in receiving yards in the close loss to Philly. The rookie has caught seven of his 11 targets for 65 scoreless yards through the first two games of the season. Tennessee will now get ready to take on the Giants in Week 3. Tate will be tough to start in fantasy until Tennessee's passing attack starts to show more life.

news.body: Carnell Tate caught four of his six targets for 38 yards in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
news.head: Carnell Tate catches four passes in Week 1
news.impact: Tate tied for the team lead in targets and receiving yards while finishing second in receptions in his NFL debut. The rookie receiver will surely have bigger games going forward, as the entire Tennessee offense struggled in the season opener. Tate will be a low-end WR3 heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Eagles.

news.body: Carnell Tate (stiffness) is off of the injury report and good to go for Week 1's matchup against the New York Jets.
news.head: Carnell Tate (stiffness) good to go for Sunday
news.impact: The rookie is no longer on Tennessee's injury report and is set to make his NFL debut on Sunday. Fantasy managers should pay close attention to his debut game to see if he has the talent and situation of a breakout fantasy player for this season.

news.body: Titans rookie WR Carnell Tate returned to practice on Friday.
news.head: Carnell Tate returns to practice Friday
news.impact: Tate missed practice time earlier this week due to "stiffness." The rookie could see some more reps in Sunday's preseason game against the Seahawks.

news.body: CeeDee Lamb caught 8-of-9 targets for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the win over the Commanders.
news.head: CeeDee Lamb finds the end zone twice in Week 2 win
news.impact: Lamb turned in an excellent performance, leading the team in receptions and receiving yards. Lamb already has three touchdowns in the first two games and will look to continue his strong start to the season against the Ravens in Week 3.

news.body: CeeDee Lamb hauled in 5-of-8 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the New York Giants.
news.head: CeeDee Lamb hauls in touchdown in loss Sunday
news.impact: Lamb was technically Dallas' leading receiver on Sunday night, but he did that with just 44 yards over the course of the game. He was able to haul in a touchdown at one point, however, which helped to salvage his fantasy total on the day. He will likely revert to being an elite producer at the position when Dallas' offense as a whole bounces back sometime within the next few weeks.

news.body: The Cowboys restructured the contract of WR CeeDee Lamb.
news.head: CeeDee Lamb has contract restructured by Cowboys
news.impact: Lamb was one of three players who had their contracts restructured to help create a significant amount of capital space for the Cowboys. They are now under the cap heading into free agency. Lamb and George Pickens are expected to run it back with Dak Prescott in the passing game for Dallas.

news.body: CeeDee Lamb caught his only target for four yards in Sunday's loss to the Giants.
news.head: CeeDee Lamb catches just one pass in Week 18
news.impact: The Cowboys limited most of their starters' snaps in Week 18, and Lamb was no exception. The four-time Pro-Bowler made his 75th catch of the season Sunday, as he finished the campaign with 1,077 yards and three touchdowns over 14 games.

news.body: Chris Godwin Jr. caught 3-of-4 targets for 25 yards in the Buccaneers 23-16 loss against the Vikings on Sunday.
news.head: Chris Godwin Jr. catches three passes Sunday
news.impact: Godwin continues to not be able to make a huge impact on the field. With Baker Mayfield also dislocating his thumb late in the loss, Godwin will be tough to trust in lineups based on his slow start to the season.

news.body: Chris Godwin Jr. caught 3-of-3 targets for 46 yards in the Buccaneers 23-19 loss against the Browns.
news.head: Chris Godwin Jr. totals 46 yards Sunday
news.impact: Godwin was mostly quiet for the second straight week as Baker Mayfield has continued to struggle. He'll be on the WR3/WR4 radar next week against the Vikings.

news.body: Chris Godwin Jr. caught 4-of-4 targets for 40 yards in the Buccaneers 33-27 loss against the Bengals on Sunday.
news.head: Chris Godwin Jr. hauls in four passes Sunday
news.impact: Godwin totaled 30 of his 40 yards on one reception. The Bucs offense was unable to get in sync with four lost fumbles. He'll remain a WR3 heading into Week 2 against the Browns.

news.body: Chris Godwin Jr. did not practice on Tuesday to manage injuries and soreness.
news.head: Chris Godwin Jr. (soreness) does not practice Tuesday
news.impact: Godwin, Jalen McMillan and Emeka Egbuka all sat out on Tuesday. It doesn't appear to be anything serious with any of them.

news.body: Chris Olave caught 8-of-10 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in the Saints 24-17 win over the Ravens.
news.head: Chris Olave finds the end zone in Week 2 win
news.impact: Olave was considered questionable to play due to a hamstring injury, but that did not appear to impact him at all against the Ravens. Olave caught a 21-yard touchdown pass in the fourth quarter to tie the game and help pace the Saints to the upset win. Olave will look to continue his strong start to the season in Week 3 against Las Vegas.

news.body: Saints WR Chris Olave (hamstring) is officially active for a Week 2 matchup with the Ravens.
news.head: Chris Olave (hamstring) officially active for Week 2
news.impact: Olave was a late addition to the injury report this week and was listed as questionable to play in Week 2. He immediately becomes the top pass catching option for QB Tyler Shough and the Saints.

news.body: Chris Olave (hamstring) is expected to play on Sunday against Baltimore.
news.head: Chris Olave (hamstring) expected to play against Baltimore
news.impact: This is great news for the Saints, who are already down Jordyn Tyson. If Olave sits, Devaughn Vele and Juwan Johnson would be the primary options for Tyler Shough in the passing game. They're worth starting whether or not Olave plays, but the extra defensive attention given to them if he sits could cap their ceilings a little.

news.body: Chris Olave has been listed as questionable for Sunday’s game against the Ravens.
news.head: Chris Olave (hamstring) listed questionable for Week 2
news.impact: Olave was able to practice on Friday after he was a late addition to the injury report on Thursday. He should be on the favorable side of questionable, but he'll still need to be monitored on Sunday ahead of kickoff.

news.body: Christian Watson caught 7 of 10 targets for 96 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday.
news.head: Christian Watson extends touchdown streak to three games
news.impact: It might not have been in a win, but fantasy managers won't care. Watson has been a clear favorite target for Jordan Love, especially down in the red zone, with Tucker Kraft still working his way back to full health. He should be in your lineup whenever he is playing.

news.body: Christian Watson hauled in four of his team-high 11 targets for 41 yards and one touchdown in the Packers' 20-17 Week 2 win over the New York Jets.
news.head: Christian Watson finds end zone in Week 2 win over Jets
news.impact: Watson has been impactful as part of an inconsistent Green Bay offense to begin the season, catching one or more touchdowns on eight or more targets in each of the first two games. The wideout offers fantasy managers one of the few stable options in an underperforming Packer offense ahead of a favorable Week 3 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

news.body: Christian Watson caught 6-of-8 targets for 147 yards and two touchdowns in the Packers 39-22 loss against the Vikings on Sunday.
news.head: Christian Watson scores two touchdowns in big day Sunday
news.impact: Watson exploded for an 81-yard catch and run score early. He was later found in the end zone again by Jordan Love. He will be an upside WR2 next week against the Jets.

news.body: Christian Watson has agreed to a four-year, $110 million extension with the Green Bay Packers. He is the second Green Bay receiver to sign an extension this offseason following Jayden Reed.
news.head: Christian Watson agrees to four-year, $110 million extension with Packers
news.impact: Watson put together his best season on a per game basis in 2025 after coming back from an injury that forced him to miss the first seven weeks of the season. It’s quite a lot of money for a receiver who has been plagued with health issues and never had more than 620 receiving yards in a year. But to be fair to him, he averaged 13.2 PPR PPG in 2025 and he’s seen by many as a sleeper in 2026. This could certainly be the year he comes alive for the Packers offense.

news.body: Courtland Sutton caught three of his four targets for 25 yards in a 20-13 win over the Jaguars in Week 2.
news.head: Courtland Sutton held to 25 yards in Week 2
news.impact: Sutton posted a pedestrian stat line in the Broncos' exciting comeback win. It is becoming a concern after he caught just two passes for 11 yards back in Week 1. The Broncos don't seem to be prioritizing getting him the ball as they have in past years, leaving Sutton as a risky flex option in Week 3 against the Rams.

news.body: Courtland Sutton caught 2-of-5 targets for just 11 yards in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.head: Courtland Sutton uninvolved in loss Monday
news.impact: Denver's offense as a whole struggled heavily on Monday night, and Sutton was no exception to that. He caught just two of his five targets over the course of the game and was only able to turn that into a measly 11 yards. He remains off of the fantasy radar for the foreseeable future, even in more favorable matchups.

news.body: Courtland Sutton was seen in full pads to begin practice on Friday.
news.head: Courtland Sutton in full pads at practice Friday
news.impact: It is a positive sign after Sutton missed practice on Tuesday and Wednesday before he was limited in his return on Thursday. It appears he should be able to do more in practice on Friday.
