news.body: Broncos WR Courtland Sutton is “being limited as part of the team’s ‘protocols’ for the veteran wide receiver.”
news.head: Courtland Sutton being limited early in training camp
news.impact: It explains why Sutton was not seen practicing on Tuesday or Wednesday. He returned to practice on Thursday, but he was still held out of team drills. He should continue to be ramped up as we get closer to the season.

news.body: Davante Adams hauled in 8-of-10 targets for 195 yards and two touchdowns in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
news.head: Davante Adams dominant in win Monday
news.impact: Adams had one of his best games as a Ram on Monday night. He put up nearly 200 receiving yards in this blowout win over the Giants, and he was also able to get into the end zone on two separate occasions. He really stepped up in the absence of Puka Nacua (hip), so if he misses more time, fantasy managers should continue to view Adams as a can't-miss option any given week that he's the team's undisputed WR1.

news.body: Davante Adams caught just three of six targets for 26 yards in the Rams' 27-7 loss to the 49ers on Thursday.
news.head: Davante Adams quiet in loss to 49ers
news.impact: Adams could just not get much going against the Niners. On the bright side, his six targets were second on the team, so he's still earning opportunities. It just wasn't his day, as was the story for most of the team. He will try to improve next time out.

news.body: Rams coach Sean McVay said he “absolutely” expects to have Davante Adams back next season.
news.head: Davante Adams expected to be back with Rams next season
news.impact: Adams has one more year left on his contract as he comes off a year where he led the league in receiving touchdowns. The Rams are expected to run it back with Adams, Puka Nacua and Matthew Stafford after falling just short of the Super Bowl this year.

news.body: Davante Adams (hamstring) has been removed from the Rams' injury report.
news.head: Davante Adams (hamstring) off injury report
news.impact: Adams has been fully active at Rams' practice this week and will be ready to go for Saturday's playoff matchup with the Panthers. Adams missed the final three weeks of the regular season after hauling in 60 passes, including a league-leading 14 touchdown grabs, over 14 games.

news.body: Deebo Samuel Sr. recorded an 80-yard touchdown on a lateral in the 49ers 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
news.head: Deebo Samuel Sr. scores long touchdown Sunday
news.impact: Samuel took a lateral from Mike Evans to the house for an 80-yard touchdown in the opening drive. He could see more involvement next week if Mike Evans (rib) misses time.

news.body: Deebo Samuel Sr. caught 3-of-4 targets for 31 yards, adding four yards on one carry in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
news.head: Deebo Samuel Sr. finished with three receptions in Week 2
news.impact: Samuel fell well short of the 60 total yards and a touchdown he contributed in Week 1, but he was still significantly involved in Week 2. That should remain the case as long as the veteran playmaker is healthy. Samuel has secured 9-of-11 targets for 79 yards through two games. He's also carried the ball once in each contest, gaining 16 yards.

news.body: Deebo Samuel Sr. caught six of seven targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers' 27-7 win over the Rams on Thursday. He also carried the ball once for 12 yards.
news.head: Deebo Samuel Sr. snags touchdown in win
news.impact: Samuel looks to have come back to his old role on the 49ers, lining up everywhere and getting the ball put in his hands to make plays. He even had over 70 kick return yards. Samuel just might be a draft-day steal if they are going to use him like this throughout the season.

news.body: 49ers WR Deebo Samuel Sr. will play against the Chargers in the preseason
news.head: Deebo Samuel Sr. starting against Chargers
news.impact: Thursday night's contest could offer a closer look at the type of role Samuel will have in the 49ers' offense this season.

news.body: Denzel Boston caught 5-of-7 targets for 95 yards and a touchdown in the Browns 23-19 win over the Buccaneers.
news.head: Denzel Boston snags another touchdown Sunday
news.impact: Boston connected with Deshaun Watson on a touchdown for the second straight week. He is seemingly emerging as the clear WR1 on the Browns offense. He'll hold some upside WR3 appeal next week for fantasy managers against the Panthers.

news.body: Denzel Boston caught two of four targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
news.head: Denzel Boston snags bomb touchdown in loss
news.impact: Boston had the Browns' only touchdown, though sadly it was in garbage time. His four targets tied with Jerry Jeudy for second on the team, an encouraging sign for his future usage as he gets further acclimated to the NFL game.

news.body: Browns coach Todd Monken said rookie WR Denzel Boston will move into first-team offense.
news.head: Denzel Boston to practice with first-team offense
news.impact: Boston continues to show out early on in training camp. He is slated to compete for an immediate starting role.

news.body: The Cleveland Browns have selected WR Denzel Boston with the No. 39 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
news.head: Denzel Boston selected No. 39 by Cleveland Browns
news.impact: Boston becomes the second wide receiver taken by the Browns in the first two rounds of the 2026 Draft as they double up after selecting KC Concepcion in the first round Thursday. Boston is a much larger receiver (6-3, 212) out of Washington and led the Huskies in receiving yards last season. He did not run a 40-yard dash at the combine and doesn't display top speed to create separation. But, he does have excellent hands and he was very tough to bring down at the collegiate level. It's a little surprising that the Browns took another receiver with a need for offensive line help. But, Cleveland is looking for playmakers to improve the offense in 2026 and Boston should help with that as part of the receiver rotation.

news.body: Devaughn Vele caught 5-of-7 targets for 64 yards in the Saints 24-17 win over the Ravens.
news.head: Devaughn Vele hauls in five passes in Week 2 win
news.impact: Vele has put together two solid games to open the season, tallying 12 receptions on 16 targets. Vele is the clear WR2 in the Saints' offense and should be poised for another strong performance against the Raiders in Week 3.

news.body: Devaughn Vele hauled in seven of his nine targets for 69 yards and one touchdown in the Saints' 31-30 Week 1 loss to the Detroit Lions.
news.head: Devaughn Vele finds end zone in Week 1 loss to Lions
news.impact: Vele capitalized on a sizeable role in the New Orleans passing attack, finishing second in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in a losing effort. The wideout looks poised to offer head coach Kellen Moore another impactful pass-catching option in the New Orleans offense moving forward, with a Week 2 contest against the Baltimore Ravens up next.

news.body: The Saints placed Devaughn Vele on injured reserve.
news.head: Devaughn Vele (shoulder) placed on IR
news.impact: Vele will miss the rest of the season. He finishes the year having caught 25 passes for 293 yards and two touchdowns after being traded to the Saints mid-season.

news.body: Devaughn Vele (shoulder) has been ruled out for the Saints game against the Jets on Sunday.
news.head: Devaughn Vele (shoulder) out on Sunday against Jets
news.impact: Vele was having a bit of a breakout the last few weeks, but that is now on hold. Mason Tipton will likely fill the WR2 role in the offense, but the vacated targets will likely find their way to Chris Olave, Juwan Johnson, and the running backs than Tipton himself seeing a large bump in usage.

news.body: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is off of the injury report and cleared to play for the Philadelphia Eagles against the Chicago Bears Monday night.
news.head: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) cleared for Week 3
news.impact: Smith is good to go for head coach Nick Sirianni after logging practice sessions on back-to-back days to end the week while battling a lingering hamstring injury, offering quarterback Jalen Hurts is primary pass-catching target against a shaky Bears secondary Monday night.

news.body: DeVonta Smith is participating in practice on Friday.
news.head: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) now practicing Friday
news.impact: Smith was not wearing his jersey at the start of practice, but he is now taking part in drills. It is a good sign for his status ahead of Monday's game against the Bears.

news.body: DeVonta Smith was seen without his jersey at practice on Friday.
news.head: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) not wearing jersey at practice Friday
news.impact: Smith did take part in the stretching period during practice. His status will need to be monitored in practice on Saturday ahead of Monday's game against the Bears.

news.body: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) did not take part in Thursday's practice session.
news.head: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) did not practice Thursday
news.impact: Smith delivered a huge game for the Eagles in this past Sunday's win over the Titans, but he has reportedly been dealing with a hamstring issue at practice this week. Smith did not practice Thursday, but he still seems likely to play Monday. This is a situation to be aware of, however.

news.body: DJ Moore hauled in six of his 10 targets for 67 yards in the Bills' 24-16 Week 3 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: DJ Moore leads pass-catchers in Week 3 win over Chargers
news.impact: Moore has been impactful to begin the season, finishing with over 65 receiving yards in two of the first three contests. The wideout remains locked in as a dynamic pass-catching option for quarterback Josh Allen, with a Week 4 matchup against the New England Patriots ahead.

news.body: DJ Moore (shoulder) is officially active for Week 3 for the Buffalo Bills against the Los Angeles Chargers according to Ian Rapoport.
news.head: DJ Moore (shoulder) active for Week 3
news.impact: Moore is good to go after not battling any setbacks during pregame activities, boosting a Buffalo passing attack that will look to push the envelope against the Chargers Sunday.

news.body: Bills WR DJ Moore (shoulder) is expected to play today against the Chargers.
news.head: DJ Moore (shoulder) expected to play today
news.impact: Moore is currently listed as questionable due to a shoulder injury he suffered in Week 2. He was able to shed the non-contact practice jersey Friday and appears to be a full go for the Bills Sunday.

news.body: DJ Moore is listed as questionable for Sunday’s game against the Chargers.
news.head: DJ Moore (shoulder) listed questionable Sunday
news.impact: Moore returned to practice in a non-contact jersey on Friday. His status will need to be monitored closer to kickoff on Sunday.

news.body: DK Metcalf caught 3-of-5 targets for 31 yards and a touchdown in a 30-27 win over the Bengals.
news.head: DK Metcalf hauls in first TD pass in Week 3 win
news.impact: Metcalf found the end zone on a six-yard connection with Aaron Rodgers in the third quarter. The yardage totals and receptions have not been there for Metcalf yet this season, but he will look for an uptick in production against the Browns in Week 4.

news.body: Steelers WR DK Metcalf caught 4-of-9 targets for 27 yards in a 20-3 loss to the Patriots.
news.head: DK Metcalf leads team in targets in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Metcalf was shadowed by Patriots DB Christian Gonzalez for the majority of the game, limiting his production and forcing Aaron Rodgers to look elsewhere. Metcalf has lead the team in targets in the first two games, so the target volume is encouraging, fantasy managers are just waiting for it to result in more production. Metcalf and the Steelers will take on the Bengals in Week 3.

news.body: DK Metcalf caught four of his 10 targets for 40 yards in a 20-13 win over the Falcons in Week 1.
news.head: DK Metcalf leads Steelers with 10 targets in Week 1
news.impact: Metcalf didn't do much damage but his usage was encouraging as he easily led the Steelers in targets while newcomer Michael Pittman Jr. saw just three looks from Aaron Rodgers. Metcalf will be a high-end WR3 in fantasy heading into Week 2 against the Patriots.

news.body: DK Metcalf is off of the injury report for Week 1's matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.
news.head: DK Metcalf off injury report for Week 1
news.impact: Metcalf was dealing with an undisclosed injury earlier, but it's not an issue for him anymore and he is off of the injury report entirely ahead of Week 1. He goes into the season as the projected top target for the Steelers this season.

news.body: Dontayvion Wicks caught five of his six targets for 74 yards in a 24-20 win over the Titans in Week 2.
news.head: Dontayvion Wicks goes for 74 yards in Week 2
news.impact: Wicks finished second on the Eagles in all receiving categories in the close win. The veteran wideout could stay involved as the Eagles lost Dallas Goedert to a knee injury in the game. Wicks is on the radar as a flex option in fantasy heading into Week 3 against the Bears.

news.body: Dontayvion Wicks hauled in two of his four targets for 73 yards and one touchdown in the Eagles’ 24-22 Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders.
news.head: Dontayvion Wicks finds end zone in Week 1 win
news.impact: Wicks made the most of his modest target share in the season opener, averaging 36.5 yards per reception in the win. The wideout offers head coach Nick Sirianni another explosive pass-catching option moving forward, with a favorable Week 2 matchup against the Tennessee Titans up next.

news.body: Dontayvion Wicks is trending towards opening the season as the No. 2 wide receiver for the Eagles to open the season.
news.head: Dontayvion Wicks on track to be Eagles WR2
news.impact: Wicks continues to impress during training camp, while rookie Makai Lemon misses time with a hamstring injury. He was able to show flashes in Green Bay and could see more consistent opportunity with the Eagles. He'll remain a player to monitor for fantasy managers as well as the health of Lemon.

news.body: Dontayvion Wicks was absent Wednesday at Eagles OTAs.
news.head: Dontayvion Wicks not at Eagles OTAs Wednesday
news.impact: Wicks was acquired by the Eagles in a trade this offseason. He will figure to compete for an immediate role in the Eagles wide receiver room.

news.body: Drake London caught 9 of 10 targets for 194 yards in the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
news.head: Drake London goes for 194 yards in win over Green Bay
news.impact: London was fantastic in this game, spurred on by the return of Michael Penix. When Penix has been at the helm of the offense, London has been among the best fantasy producers in the game, and it showed once again on Thursday. He should be a locked in starter whenever Penix is playing.

news.body: Drake London caught four of five targets for 51 yards in the Falcons' 34-3 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
news.head: Drake London quiet in loss to Panthers
news.impact: London had a better game than last week, but it still is nowhere near what you drafted him to do. The Falcons' quarterback play has been abysmal so far, which is the primary contributor to his struggles. But hopefully Michael Penix can fix things if he can return on Thursday.

news.body: Drake London caught two of his four targets for 29 yards in a 20-13 loss to the Steelers in Week 1. He also gained six yards on his lone carry in the game.
news.head: Drake London held to two catches in Week 1 loss
news.impact: London was quiet in the close loss, although his 29 receiving yards were good enough for him to finish second on the Falcons in that category. The Falcons were forced to play Cooper Rush, their third-string QB, thanks to injuries, so London should bounce back once either Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix is ready to return to the field. London sets up as a low-end WR1 heading into Week 2 against Carolina.

news.body: Falcons GM Ian Cunningham said an extension for Drake London is “on top of mind.”
news.head: Drake London: Extension is 'on top of mind' per GM Ian Cunningham
news.impact: It appears an extension could be agreed to after the NFL Draft. London is entering the final year of his rookie contract. There should be a new deal agreed to at some point later in the offseason.

news.body: Emeka Egbuka caught 5-of-9 targets for 62 yards in the Buccaneers 23-16 loss against the Vikings on Sunday.
news.head: Emeka Egbuka totals 62 yards Sunday
news.impact: Egbuka was the leading receiver for Tampa Bay on the day. He has still yet to have one of his huge explosive games. The status of Baker Mayfield will need to be monitored after he left the game late with a dislocated thumb.

news.body: Emeka Egbuka caught 3-of-5 targets for 16 yards and a touchdown in the Buccaneers 23-19 loss against the Browns.
news.head: Emeka Egbuka has touchdown salvage performance Sunday
news.impact: It would have been a disastrous afternoon for Egbuka if it weren't for a touchdown he hauled in. He'll remain a WR2 play next week against the Vikings.

news.body: Emeka Egbuka caught 5-of-6 targets for 63 yards in the Buccaneers 33-27 loss against the Bengals on Sunday.
news.head: Emeka Egbuka totals 63 yards Sunday
news.impact: Egbuka entered Sunday fully healthy after coming off a toe injury. He got off to a strong start in the first half, but he was not targeted in the second half despite the Bucs trailing. He remains a WR2 heading into Week 2.

news.body: Emeka Egbuka (toe) is cleared to play in Week 1 for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers against the Cincinnati Bengals according to Greg Auman.
news.head: Emeka Egbuka (toe) cleared for Week 1

news.body: Garrett Wilson caught 10-of-13 targets for 107 yards and a touchdown in a 31-24 loss to the Lions.
news.head: Garrett Wilson hauls in 10 passes in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Wilson caught a 24-yard strike from Geno Smith in the fourth quarter to tie the game. Fantasy managers will want to monitor Wilson's status early in the week as he did exit with an injury on the final drive. Wilson and the Jets will take on the Bears in Week 4.

news.body: Garrett Wilson exited Sunday’s contest between the New York Jets and Detroit Lions with an apparent injury.
news.head: Garrett Wilson exits Sunday
news.impact: Wilson was seen limping to the sideline late in the fourth quarter for head coach Aaron Glenn, hauling in 10 of his team-leading 13 targets for 107 yards and one touchdown before exiting.

news.body: Garrett Wilson hauled in five of his seven targets for 57 yards and one touchdown in the Jets' 20-17 Week 2 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
news.head: Garrett Wilson finds end zone in Week 2 loss to Packers
news.impact: Wilson continues to make the most of sizeable involvement in an underperforming passing attack to begin the season, recording five or more receptions in each of the first two games. The wideout remains one of the more impactful options as part of a Jets offense filled with more questions than answers early on ahead of a Week 3 contest against the Detroit Lions.

news.body: Garrett Wilson caught six of his seven targets for 79 yards in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 1.
news.head: Garrett Wilson goes for 79 yards in Week 1
news.impact: Wilson led the Jets in all receiving categories in the easy win over an overmatched Tennessee team. Even though it wasn't a huge performance from Wilson, it was an encouraging debut for the receiver with Geno Smith at the helm. Wilson settles in as a high-end WR2 in a Week 2 home matchup against the Packers.

news.body: George Pickens caught 6-of-8 targets for 40 yards in the Cowboys in a win over the Commanders.
news.head: George Pickens hauls in six passes in Week 2
news.impact: Pickens had a much needed bounce back performance after tallying just three receptions. Although Pickens has not found the endzone yet this season, the increase in targets and receptions over the first week is a strong sign that Pickens will remain a factor in this offense. The Cowboys will take on the Ravens in Week 3.

news.body: George Pickens caught 3-of-6 targets for just 28 yards in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the New York Giants.
news.head: George Pickens held to 28 yards Sunday
news.impact: Pickens had an extremely disappointing start to the season on Sunday night. He was held to just 28 yards on three catches in the team's first game of the season after being hyped up as an elite fantasy prospect throughout the preseason. He should bounce back and play better than this moving forward, but his week-to-week floor may be lower than some realize if Dallas' offense struggles with consistency this season.

news.body: George Pickens will officially play the 2026 season on a $27.3 million franchise tag for the Dallas Cowboys.
news.head: George Pickens to play 2026 season on franchise tag with Cowboys
news.impact: Pickens and the Cowboys could not agree upon a long-term extension this summer, so he will head into the year effectively on a 1-year deal. The wideout is coming off a career year in which he hauled in 93 catches for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns. He will head into this season with Dallas firmly in the WR1 conversation in fantasy.

news.body: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said he plans to move WR George Pickens around the formation more this season.
news.head: George Pickens expected to move around formation more this season
news.impact: Pickens has reported to mandatory minicamp after sitting out of voluntary OTAs. He is expected to play both on the outside and in the slot, adding to the versatility he will offer the Cowboys offense.

news.body: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) is good to go for Sunday's game against the New England Patriots.
news.head: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) good to go for Sunday
news.impact: As expected, the veteran wideout's thumb injury is not a serious issue for him and he will play through it on Sunday. He will be up against his former team on Sunday, but fantasy managers still shouldn't consider him a trustworthy option in that interesting matchup.

news.body: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) listed as limited Wednesday
news.impact: The veteran should be fine to play in Week 3, despite being limited at practice all week so far. Barring any setbacks with his recovery, he should be a full go against his former team on Sunday but still doesn't project to be a strong option from a fantasy perspective.

news.body: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) a limited participant Wednesday
news.impact: A thumb injury left Meyers limited at Jacksonville's first practice of the week on Wednesday. It doesn't seem likely to affect his availability for Week 3, however, and he should continue to play his usual role in a matchup against his former team, the Patriots, this week if he suffers no setbacks in his recovery.

news.body: Jakobi Meyers caught his lone target for a 28-yard gain in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
news.head: Jakobi Meyers held to one catch in Week 2
news.impact: Meyers didn't record his lone catch of the game until the fourth quarter as he took a backseat to both Parker Washington and Brian Thomas Jr. Meyers has now caught all three of his targets for 68 yards and a touchdown through two games this season. He will be a flex consideration heading into Week 3 against the Patriots.

news.body: Panthers WR Jalen Coker (quad) has been ruled out for the remainder of the game against Cleveland.
news.head: Jalen Coker (quad) out for the remainder of Week 3
news.impact: Coker was questionable to play today but that was due to an ankle injury. Coker has now picked up a new injury and will not return. He will finish the day with 18 receiving yards on two receptions.

news.body: Panthers WR Jalen Coker (ankle) is officially active for Week 3.
news.head: Jalen Coker (ankle) officially active for Week 3
news.impact: Coker was considered questionable after suffering an ankle injury in Week 2. With Xavier Legette inactive, Coker and Tetairoa McMillan should see plenty of targets against Cleveland.

news.body: Jalen Coker is on the field for warmups and is expected to play.
news.head: Jalen Coker (ankle) expected to play on Sunday
news.impact: Coker came out of Week 2 with an ankle injury but it looks like he is going to play. He will provide Bryce Young another reliable target alongside of Tetairoa McMillan against the Browns. Start him as a WR2 with upside.

news.body: Jalen Coker has been listed as questionable for Sunday’s game against the Browns.
news.head: Jalen Coker (ankle) listed questionable Sunday
news.impact: Coker returned to practice on Friday. He appears to be trending in the right direction. He'll remain an upside WR3 play for fantasy managers.

news.body: Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Raiders 35-27 win over the Saints on Sunday.
news.head: Jalen Nailor catches one pass Sunday
news.impact: Nailor remains uninvolved in the offense with Las Vegas. He remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

news.body: Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-3 targets for nine yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: Jalen Nailor quiet in win Sunday
news.impact: Nailor was a non-factor on Sunday. He caught just one pass against the Chargers and wasn't able to do much of note with it. He isn't expected to be a good fantasy option moving forward, especially with Brock Bowers (knee) set to return to the lineup in the very near future.

news.body: Jalen Nailor caught three of his five targets for 27 yards in the Raiders' 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 1.
news.head: Jalen Nailor catches three passes in Week 1
news.impact: Nailor was one of many that saw involvement in the Las Vegas passing offense, finishing as one of six to catch at least one pass in the win. The wideout will look to offer more impactful potential in a revamped Las Vegas offense as the season moves forward, with a Week 2 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

news.body: The Raiders agreed to terms with WR Jalen Nailor on a three-year, $35 million contract.
news.head: Jalen Nailor signs three-year deal with Raiders
news.impact: Nailor will receive $23 million in guaranteed money. He is looking to step into a bigger role after playing in a limited role in Minnesota. He will be a late-round flier in drafts for now.

news.body: Ja'Marr Chase caught 9-of-12 targets for 98 yards and a touchdown in a 30-27 loss to the Steelers.
news.head: Ja'Marr Chase excellent in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Chase led the team in all of the receiving categories for the Bengals Sunday. Chase and Joe Burrow connected on a three-yard touchdown strike in the first quarter. Chase and the Bengals will take on the Jaguars in Week 4.

news.body: Ja'Marr Chase caught 7-of-9 targets for 75 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals 20-6 win over the Texans on Sunday.
news.head: Ja'Marr Chase hauls in two touchdowns Sunday
news.impact: Chase recorded both of the touchdowns scored by Cincinnati on Sunday, including an incredible catch where he just barely got both feet in. He remains a locked and loaded WR1 heading into next week against the Steelers.

news.body: Ja'Marr Chase caught 2-of-4 targets for 12 yards in the Bengals 33-27 win over the Buccaneers.
news.head: Ja'Marr Chase very quiet to open season
news.impact: It was a Week 1 to forget for Chase fantasy managers to say the least. There shouldn't be too much of concern after one week, though he draws an even tougher matchup in Week 2 against the Texans.

news.body: Ja’Marr Chase (knee) has been cleared to play in Week 1 for the Cincinnati Bengals against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers according to Kelsey Conway.
news.head: Ja’Marr Chase (knee) cleared for Week 1

news.body: Jameson Williams caught 4-of-4 targets for 49 yards in a 31-24 win over the Jets.
news.head: Jameson Williams hauls in four passes in Week 3 win
news.impact: Williams took a back seat in the offense Sunday with Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs dominating the targets against the Jets. Williams will look to become more involved in the offense in a Week 4 matchup with the Panthers.

news.body: Jameson Williams caught 2-of-4 targets for 33 yards in Thursday night's 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Jameson Williams underwhelming in loss Thursday
news.impact: Williams had another disappointing performance on Thursday night. He caught just two passes in this matchup against the Bills and was only able to turn that into 33 scoreless yards, leaving him with a poor fantasy total on the night. Fantasy managers should recognize his low week-to-week floor when determining whether or not to start him in any given game moving forward.

news.body: Jameson Williams caught four of his nine targets for 45 yards in the Lions' 31-30 win over the New Orleans Saints in Week 1.
news.head: Jameson Williams sees nine targets in Week 1 win
news.impact: Williams would have offered even more of an explosive impact if not for a couple of deep throw drops on passes from quarterback Jared Goff. The wideout remains a high-impact, explosive pass-catching option for fantasy managers ahead of a Week 2 road contest against the Buffalo Bills.

news.body: Jameson Williams resumed practicing on Wednesday.
news.head: Jameson Williams (shoulder) returns to practice
news.impact: Williams missed the Lions’ last two practices. He made his way back on Wednesday.

news.body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 9 of 11 targets for 155 yards and three touchdowns in the Seahawks' 31-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba has hat trick of touchdowns in win
news.impact: JSN has been on an absolute tear to start the season, with 277 yards through the first two games. He's looking QB-proof at the moment, and as long as Drew Lock can continue to get him the ball with Sam Darnold still out, JSN is an auto start. Not that you were sitting him anyway. He gets a great matchup against the Commanders next week.

news.body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 8-of-11 targets for 122 yards and a touchdown in Wednesday night's 13-10 win over the New England Patriots.
news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba electric in win Wednesday
news.impact: On Wednesday, Smith-Njigba picked up right where he left off last season, exploding for 122 yards and a touchdown in a big win over the Patriots. He did that with Drew Lock throwing him passes after starter Sam Darnold went down with a hip injury earlier in the game. Fantasy managers should be happy with his performance in this matchup but should keep a close eye on the health of Darnold, as the young wideout's week-to-week ceiling will certainly take a hit if their starting QB misses significant time.

news.body: The Seahawks signed WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba to a four-year, $168.6 million contract extension.
news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba signs historic four-year extension with Seahawks
news.impact: Smith-Njigba signs the richest contract extension for a receiver in NFL history with the deal including $120 million in guaranteed money. The 2025 NFL Offensive Player of the Year and Super Bowl Champion went for 1,793 yards and 10 touchdowns on 119 receptions last season. He will remain under contract with the Seahawks through the 2031 season.

news.body: The Seahawks exercised WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s fifth-year team option for 2027.
news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba has fifth-year team option exercised by Seahawks
news.impact: Henderson added that Smith-Njigba’s 2027 salary is fully guaranteed and should make him roughly $23.85 million. This is expected to be a step towards the two sides agreeing to a long-term extension.

news.body: Jaylen Waddle caught eight of his 10 targets for 138 yards in a 20-13 win over the Jaguars in Week 2.
news.head: Jaylen Waddle bounces back in Week 2
news.impact: Waddle led the Broncos in all receiving categories in the close win. More importantly, he bounced back after catching just one pass for two yards in Week 1. Waddle will be a solid WR2 heading into Week 3 against the Rams.

news.body: Jaylen Waddle caught 1-of-3 targets for just two yards in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.head: Jaylen Waddle disappoints in Broncos debut Monday
news.impact: There has been a lot of hype for the veteran wideout after the Broncos traded for him this offseason, but he got off to a poor start with his new team on Monday night. He caught one pass for just two yards over the course of the game, which burned any fantasy manager who risked starting him in this matchup. Denver's offense as a whole struggled heavily against Kansas City's defense, however, so there's a good chance that he and the rest of the offense bounce back and return to solid fantasy production in easier matchups moving forward.

news.body: Jaylen Waddle is in full pads at practice on Tuesday.
news.head: Jaylen Waddle (leg) in full pads at practice Tuesday
news.impact: It is another positive sign for Waddle following his return to practice on Monday. He remains on track to be good to go for the start of the regular season.

news.body: Jaylen Waddle returned to practice on Monday after dealing with a leg muscle strain.
news.head: Jaylen Waddle (leg) returns to practice Monday
news.impact: Waddle missed practice all of last week, but has now returned to action at the start of this week. The wideout should still be monitored throughout the week to see if an injury pops back up.

news.body: Jaylin Noel caught both of his targets for 17 yards in a 19-17 loss to the Colts.
news.head: Jaylin Noel hauls in two passes in Week 3
news.impact: Noel saw his target share drop from his five targets in Week 2. Fantasy managers can leave the 24-year-old on the waiver wire heading into Week 4.

news.body: Jaylin Noel caught 1-of-5 targets for 31 yards in the Texans 20-6 loss against the Bengals on Sunday.
news.head: Jaylin Noel catches one pass Sunday
news.impact: Noel was one of six players to see at least five targets for Houston on Sunday. He remains off the fantasy radar in his current role with the ball being spread around.

news.body: Jaylin Noel hauled in both of his targets for 53 yards in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.head: Jaylin Noel shows big-play ability on limited targets
news.impact: Noel only got two looks from C.J. Stroud on Sunday, but he had the longest gain of the day with a 35-yard pickup. The second-year receiver out of Iowa State has big-play potential every week, but he may not see enough volume to move beyond being a boom-or-bust fantasy option.

news.body: Jaylin Noel returned to practice on Tuesday.
news.head: Jaylin Noel (hamstring/finger) returns to practice
news.impact: Noel returns from hamstring and finger injuries. He is expected to hold a depth role in the Texans wide receiver room.

news.body: Jordan Addison caught 5-of-9 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings 23-16 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
news.head: Jordan Addison leads the way for Vikings Sunday
news.impact: Addison took on a bigger role with Justin Jefferson (ankle) exiting early. He hauled in a 41-yard touchdown pass from Kyler Murray. He'll jump into a WR2/WR3 play next week against the Dolphins if Jefferson is sidelined.

news.body: Jordan Addison hauled in two of his five targets for 21 yards in the Vikings' 9-3 Week 2 win over the Chicago Bears.
news.head: Jordan Addison sees five targets in Week 2 win
news.impact: Addison has struggled to make an impact as part of an underwhelming Minnesota passing attack to begin the season, finishing with two receptions or less in each of the first two games. The wideout remains a high-risk pass-catching option in all formats ahead of a Week 3 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

news.body: Jordan Addison did not catch either of his two targets in the Vikings 39-22 win over the Packers.
news.head: Jordan Addison fails to catch pass Sunday
news.impact: Justin Jefferson dominated the targets after Carson Wentz took over behind center. Addison will be in the WR3/WR4 mix heading into Week 2 against a vulnerable Bears defense.

news.body: Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said WR Jordan Addison will miss a day or two after jamming his thumb.
news.head: Jordan Addison (thumb) to miss day or two of practice
news.impact: Addison underwent tests that showed the injury will be short-term. He could return to practice by this weekend.

news.body: Josh Downs caught 5-of-11 targets for 77 yards in a 19-17 win over Houston.
news.head: Josh Downs hauls in five passes in Week 3 win
news.impact: Downs led the team in receiving yards and targets in the win over Houston. With Alec Pierce (heel) on injured reserve, fantasy managers should expect Downs to continue to see plenty of targets from Daniel Jones. Downs and the Colts will take on the Commanders in Week 4.

news.body: Josh Downs hauled in 7-of-9 targets for 72 yards in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.head: Josh Downs leads team in receiving Sunday
news.impact: The Colts needed Downs to step up on Sunday night, and he did just that, delivering a team-high 72 yards in a narrow loss to the Chiefs. He seems primed to improve as a fantasy option in the near future with Alec Pierce (heel) seemingly set to miss some time after aggravating an injury.

news.body: Josh Downs caught two of his four targets for 37 yards in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 1.
news.head: Josh Downs catches two passes in Week 1
news.impact: Downs saw modest involvement in an underperforming Indianapolis passing attack, finishing third on the team in targets in the loss. The wideout remains one of the more risky pass-catchers entering a difficult Week 2 contest against the Kansas City Chiefs.

news.body: Josh Downs (calf) is without an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Baltimore Ravens.
news.head: Josh Downs (calf) without injury designation for Sunday
news.impact: Downs is not listed on Indianapolis' injury report heading into Week 1, meaning that his calf injury is no longer an issue and that he should be at full health at this point. Indianapolis' distribution of targets should be something fantasy managers keep a close eye on this weekend, but the 25-year old isn't projected to be a strong fantasy asset on his own to start the season.

news.body: Justin Jefferson (ankle) is questionable to return for the Minnesota Vikings against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers Sunday.
news.head: Justin Jefferson (ankle) questionable to return Sunday
news.impact: Jefferson headed to the locker room late in the second quarter with the ankle injury, hauling in both of his targets for 32 yards before exiting. Jordan Addison steps into a No. 1 role with Jefferson sidelined.

news.body: Justin Jefferson hauled in three of his six targets for a team-high 55 yards in the Vikings' 9-3 Week 2 win over the Chicago Bears.
news.head: Justin Jefferson leads pass-catchers in Week 2 win over Bears
news.impact: Jefferson has made the most of generous involvement in an inconsistent Minnesota passing attack to begin the season, finishing with over 50 receiving yards in each of the first two games. The superstar wideout continues to fall victim to underwhelming quarterback play, with a Week 3 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers up next.

news.body: Justin Jefferson caught 8-of-9 targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns in the Vikings 39-22 win over the Packers.
news.head: Justin Jefferson scores two touchdowns Sunday
news.impact: Despite Kyler Murray leaving in the first quarter with a concussion, Jefferson was still able to produce in a big way with Carson Wentz. He remains a locked and loaded high-end WR1.

news.body: The Vikings restructured the contract of Justin Jefferson.
news.head: Justin Jefferson restructures contract with Vikings
news.impact: Minnesota is making moves to clear salary cap space. Pelissero notes they still have work to do to get under the cap by Wednesday.

news.body: Kalif Raymond caught all five of his targets for 40 yards in the Bears' 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2.
news.head: Kalif Raymond catches five passes in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Raymond continues to make the most of solid involvement in the Chicago passing attack to begin the season, recording five or more receptions in each of the first two games. The wideout continues to take advantage of his familiarity with head coach Ben Johnson's offense, with a Week 3 contest against the Philadelphia Eagles up next.

news.body: Kalif Raymond hauled in eight of his team-leading nine targets for 84 yards in the Bears' 59-37 Week 1 win over the Carolina Panthers.
news.head: Kalif Raymond leads pass-catchers in Week 1 win over Panthers
news.impact: Raymond made an immediate impact after rejoining his former offensive coordinator in the offseason, finishing first in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in the win. The wideout remains one of many dynamic options in a crowded wide receiver room, with a Week 2 contest against the Minnesota Vikings up next.

news.body: The Bears signed WR Kalif Raymond.
news.head: Kalif Raymond signs with Bears
news.impact: Raymond remains in the NFC North after five seasons with the Lions. He will remain in a depth role in the Bears wide receiver room.

news.body: Kalif Raymond caught three passes for 52 yards and added three punt returns for 33 yards in the Lions' win over the Bears in the final game of the season.
news.head: Kalif Raymond catches three passes in Week 18
news.impact: Raymond established himself as another target for Jared Goff over the last five weeks of the regular season. After catching just 13 passes over his first 10 games of the year, Raymond caught at least one pass in each of his last five games and totaled 11 receptions during the stretch.

news.body: Kayshon Boutte caught both of his targets for 21 yards in a 19-17 loss to the Colts.
news.head: Kayshon Boutte hauls in two passes in Week 3
news.impact: Boutte continues to struggle to carve out a clear role in the Houston offense, even with Nico Collins (hamstring) out of the lineup. The 24-year-old will look to improve on his season long numbers in a Week 4 matchup against a banged up Dallas' secondary.

news.body: Kayshon Boutte caught 3-of-5 targets for 37 yards in the Texans 20-6 loss against the Bengals on Sunday.
news.head: Kayshon Boutte catches three passes Sunday
news.impact: Boutte continues to learn the playback in his second game with the Texans. He remains off the fantasy radar in his current role as an upside WR4/WR5.

news.body: Kayshon Boutte caught 1-of-2 targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.head: Kayshon Boutte makes only catch in Texans debut
news.impact: Boutte was acquired from New England late in the preseason to shore up the Texans' wide receiver corps. His big-play potential is known from the last couple of years with the Patriots, but his targets were predictably limited in an offense that is still relatively new to him. Boutte is a wait-and-see bench stash in standard fantasy leagues.

news.body: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Kayshon Boutte will play in Week 1 against the Bills.
news.head: Kayshon Boutte will play in Week 1
news.impact: Boutte was acquired in a trade with the Patriots back on August 24. Ryans said he has been “picking up the playbook really well.” He'll be a deep threat on the outside for CJ Stroud.

news.body: KC Concepcion Jr. caught 6-of-6 targets for 28 yards in the Browns 23-19 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
news.head: KC Concepcion Jr. catches six passes Sunday
news.impact: Concepcion caught all six targets he saw, but they only resulted in 28 yards. Denzel Boston has appeared to emerge as the WR1 on the Browns offense.

news.body: KC Concepcion caught four of five targets for 43 yards in the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars. He also ran the ball three times for 15 yards.
news.head: KC Concepcion snags four passes in loss to Jags
news.impact: While it wasn't a massive day, it was encouraging that Concepcion got touches as both a receiver and out of the backfield, showing the team wanted to get the ball in his hands. A loss is a loss, but brighter days should be ahead for Concepcion.

news.body: KC Concepcion was back at practice on Tuesday at Browns training camp.
news.head: KC Concepcion (shoulder) returns to practice Tuesday
news.impact: Concepcion landed hard on his shoulder that forced him out of Monday's practice early. He is back one day later.

news.body: Browns rookie WR KC Concepcion is believed to have avoided a serious shoulder injury on Monday.
news.head: KC Concepcion (shoulder) avoids serious injury
news.impact: Concepcion left practice on Monday with a shoulder injury after a hard fall. The team expects him to be fine.

news.body: Keenan Allen caught 6-of-9 targets for 63 yards and a touchdown in a 19-17 win over the Texans.
news.head: Keenan Allen finds the end zone in Week 3
news.impact: Allen turned in his best performance of the season and found the end zone for the first time as a Colt. With Alec Pierce (heel) on injured reserve, fantasy managers should expect Allen to see an increase in playing time. Allen and the Colts will take on the Commanders in Week 4.

news.body: Keenan Allen caught 1-of-5 targets for just five yards in Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.head: Keenan Allen held to one catch Sunday
news.impact: The veteran saw five opportunities on Sunday night, but he was only able to haul in one catch for five yards over the course of the night. He hasn't looked very good over the first two games of the season, which mitigates a lot of the optimism surrounding him now that Alec Pierce (heel) seems set to miss time.

news.body: Keenan Allen (rest) was a full participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Keenan Allen (rest) full participant Thursday
news.impact: As expected, the veteran was a full participant at practice on Thursday after being limited on Wednesday. The team was simply limiting his workload as a load management tactic, and he should be fully good to go for Week 2. He may see more work than usual if Alec Pierce (heel) or Ashton Dulin (ankle) are sidelined against Kansas City.

news.body: Keenan Allen (rest) was officially a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Keenan Allen (rest) officially limited Wednesday
news.impact: The veteran wideout was limited at Wednesday's practice. The team is intentionally limiting his workload at the start of the practice week, however, so it's nothing that fantasy managers should be concerned with. He should play in Week 2 but projects to be a weaker fantasy option in a tough matchup against the Chiefs this week.

news.body: Kendrick Bourne caught 2-of-3 targets for 22 yards in the Cardinals 36-30 loss against the 49ers on Sunday.
news.head: Kendrick Bourne catches two passes Sunday
news.impact: Bourne has not been as involved the past two weeks after a big Week 1 performance. He remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

news.body: Kendrick Bourne caught 2-of-3 targets for just 11 yards in Sunday's 31-7 loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
news.head: Kendrick Bourne quiet in loss Sunday
news.impact: Bourne came back down to earth in Week 2 after a stellar performance in Arizona's season opener a week before. He only caught two passes for 11 yards on Sunday, but Arizona's offense as a whole struggled in this matchup against Seattle, so there's a good chance that he will bounce back and have relevance as a depth piece in most leagues sometime in the near future.

news.body: Kendrick Bourne caught all eight of his targets for 75 yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.head: Kendrick Bourne hauls in eight passes Sunday
news.impact: Well, this was surprising. Bourne outpaced both Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson in Sunday's season opener, finishing just one reception behind TE Trey McBride for the team lead. This effort should make Bourne a popular waiver claim for Week 2, but the Cardinals are headed into a tough matchup against the defending Super Bowl champs.

news.body: Kendrick Bourne is expected to see more playing time in the slot with the Cardinals.
news.head: Kendrick Bourne expected to see more snaps in slot
news.impact: Bourne signed with Arizona in free agency this offseason. He is unlikely to hold much fantasy upside outside of a bye week fill-in behind Trey McBride, Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson in the passing game.

news.body: Khalil Shakir caught one of his three targets for six yards in the Bills' 24-16 Week 3 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: Khalil Shakir quiet in Week 3 win
news.impact: Shakir struggled to make an impact Sunday, finishing with less than three receptions for the first time in three contests. The wideout remains one of many risky pass-catching options in the Buffalo offense to this point, with a Week 4 matchup against the New England Patriots up next.

news.body: Khalil Shakir caught 3-of-6 targets for 38 yards in Thursday night's 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions.
news.head: Khalil Shakir totals 38 yards in win Thursday
news.impact: The veteran wideout wasn't very impactful on Thursday night, catching just three passes for 38 yards on a night where Buffalo's offense couldn't be stopped. He isn't expected to be a strong fantasy option for the foreseeable future, although he may be primed for more work than usual for a week or two if DJ Moore (shoulder) has to miss time.

news.body: Khalil Shakir caught four of six targets for 50 yards in the Bills’ 36-31 win over Houston on Sunday.
news.head: Khalil Shakir goes for 50 yards in win
news.impact: Shakir operated as Josh Allen’s safety valve underneath with DJ Moore and Dalton Kincaid working over the top. That’s been Shakir’s role in the past, so don’t expect it to stop any time soon. His upside is capped because of it, but he’s a decent flex play in PPR formats if you need a solid floor.

news.body: Khalil Shakir will be good to go for Sunday's game against the Houston Texans.
news.head: Khalil Shakir good to go for Sunday
news.impact: Shakir was a full participant at practice on Wednesday and is expected to be fully good to go for Sunday's season opener against the Houston Texans. He is not worth starting for fantasy purposes at this point, however, especially with DJ Moore now in town for the Bills.

news.body: Ladd McConkey hauled in four of his five targets for 66 yards in the Chargers' 24-16 Week 3 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Ladd McConkey hauls in four passes in Week 3 loss to Bills
news.impact: McConkey has made the most of inconsistent involvement in the Los Angeles passing attack to begin the season, posting over 65 receiving yards in two of the first three contests. The wideout remains one of the more dynamic options in an underperforming Chargers offense early on, with a tough Week 4 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks up next.

news.body: Ladd McConkey (rib) logged a full practice session to start the week on Wednesday.
news.head: Ladd McConkey (rib) logs full practice Wednesday
news.impact: McConkey was able to play through his rib injury last week and is now a full participant to start this week, meaning that he is close to full health and should be fully good to go for Week 3. He had an underwhelming performance last week but has a chance to bounce back this week in what should be a competitive matchup against the Bills on Sunday.

news.body: Ladd McConkey caught three passes for 35 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.head: Ladd McConkey underwhelming in loss Sunday
news.impact: McConkey was able to play on Sunday, despite being questionable coming into the week due to an injury he suffered in Week 1. He didn't look very good against the Raiders, however, totaling just 35 yards over the course of the afternoon. He will likely bounce back and return to being a good fantasy option in the near future, but his consistency may be frustrating if Los Angeles' offense continues to struggle.

news.body: Chargers WR Ladd McConkey (ribs) is officially active for a Week 2 matchup with the Raiders.
news.head: Ladd McConkey (ribs) officially active for Week 2
news.impact: McConkey is dealing with a cracked rib but was pushing to play through the injury. With McConkey active, fantasy managers should expect him to operate as the top wide receiver for the Chargers in a divisional matchup with the Raiders.

news.body: Luther Burden III hauled in three of his seven targets for 32 yards in the Bears' 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2.
news.head: Luther Burden III sees seven targets in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Burden III has provided mixed results to begin the season, finishing with less than 50 receiving yards in one of the first two games. The wideout remains difficult to trust as part of an inconsistent Chicago offense early on, with a Week 3 contest against the Philadelphia Eagles up next.

news.body: Luther Burden III hauled in all five of his targets for 63 yards while also rushing once for two yards in the Bears' 59-37 Week 1 win over the Carolina Panthers.
news.head: Luther Burden III sees six touches in Week 1
news.impact: Burden III saw steady involvement in the Chicago passing attack, finishing second on the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in the win. The wideout offers head coach Ben Johnson another dynamic pass-catcher as part of an explosive Chicago offense ahead of a Week 2 divisional matchup with the Minnesota Vikings.

news.body: Luther Burden III (groin) is off of the injury report and good to go for Week 1's matchup against the Carolina Panthers.
news.head: Luther Burden III (groin) good to go for Week 1
news.impact: Burden was dealing with a groin injury earlier in the offseason, but he is fully healthy now and carries no injury designation ahead of Sunday's season opener. He should play without any restrictions and will be primed for a huge Week 1 if the Bears are without Rome Odunze (calf) for their matchup against the Panthers.

news.body: Luther Burden III was practicing on Tuesday.
news.head: Luther Burden III (groin) practices Tuesday
news.impact: Burden had returned to practice last week. He is on track to be good to go for the start of the season next week.

news.body: Makai Lemon caught his lone target for a 14-yard gain while losing five yards on his only carry in a 24-20 win over the Titans in Week 2.
news.head: Makai Lemon sees one target in Week 2
news.impact: Lemon was quiet in the close win as Philly leaned on DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks in the passing attack. Lemon now has just four catches for nine yards through two games as he looks to carve out a larger role in the Eagles' offense. He will not be a recommended fantasy option in Week 3 against the Bears.

news.body: Makai Lemon caught three of his four targets for a loss of five yards on the Eagles’ 24-22 win over the Washington Commanders in Week 1.
news.head: Makai Lemon quiet in Week 1
news.impact: Lemon struggled to find any success in the season opener, as the pass-catcher was bottled up by the Commanders defense in the win. The wideout will look for more impactful output in a favorable Week 2 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

news.body: Makai Lemon (hamstring) is back to practicing fully for the first time in weeks. He returned to practice in a limited fashion last week, and is now practicing in full.
news.head: Makai Lemon (hamstring) practicing in full on Monday
news.impact: This is huge for Lemon’s development and integration into the offense. The more reps he gets, especially as a rookie, the better. He’s looking like a potential draft steal if he can continue to stay healthy and improve his game.

news.body: Makai Lemon (hamstring) was limited at Philadelphia's practice on Thursday.
news.head: Makai Lemon (hamstring) limited at practice Thursday
news.impact: The rookie was able to make his return to practice on Thursday. He was sidelined for a little while after suffering a hamstring injury, but it seems that he is progressing well with his recovery, as the team is now letting him practice in a limited capacity. At this rate he will be ready to play in time for the team's season opener, barring any setbacks with his recovery.

news.body: Malachi Fields hauled in 2-of-6 targets for 30 yards in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: Malachi Fields hauls in two passes Monday
news.impact: The Giants were trying to get the rookie wideout the ball on Monday night, but he was only able to haul in two out of his six targets over the course of the game. He finished with just 30 yards and isn't expected to get much better over the next couple of weeks with QB Jaxson Dart (knee) seemingly set to miss some time for New York.

news.body: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-4 targets for 25 yards in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
news.head: Malachi Fields catches two passes Sunday
news.impact: The rookie saw the field a decent amount on Sunday night. He wasn't able to put up big numbers from a fantasy perspective, however, totaling just 25 yards on two catches against the Cowboys. His debut was a solid performance overall but fantasy managers shouldn't have high hopes for him for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Malachi Fields went to a side field and worked with a trainer early in Wednesday's practice.
news.head: Malachi Fields works with trainer on side field Wednesday
news.impact: Fields had a limited workload on Tuesday. The rookie remains day-to-day.

news.body: The New York Giants have selected WR Malachi Fields with the No. 74 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
news.head: Malachi Fields selected No. 74 by New York Giants
news.impact: Fields will add some size to the Giants wide receiver room standing in at 6'5. He'll have the chance to compete for an immediate role, while also adding depth in the Giants wide receiver room.

news.body: Malik Nabers (shoulder) was officially a full participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Malik Nabers (shoulder) officially a full participant Thursday
news.impact: The star wideout was able to log a full practice session on Thursday after suffering this shoulder injury last week. It shouldn't affect his availability moving forward, but his fantasy value is still expected to be lower than it was before with Jameis Winston set to be New York's starting quarterback in place of the injured Jaxson Dart (knee) moving forward.

news.body: Malik Nabers (shoulder) was seen practicing for the Giants on Thursday.
news.head: Malik Nabers (shoulder) seen practicing Thursday
news.impact: Nabers is at practice and was seen participating on Thursday. He recently suffered a shoulder injury, but it looks like he is going to be able to play through it in Week 3, barring any setbacks between now and then. Fantasy managers should keep tabs on his status throughout the week.

news.body: Malik Nabers (shoulder) was officially limited at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Malik Nabers (shoulder) officially limited Wednesday
news.impact: Nabers is nursing a shoulder injury that he suffered in Week 2 and was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday as a result. It looks likely that he will play through it in Week 3, but fantasy managers should still continue to monitor updates about his health throughout the rest of the week.

news.body: Malik Nabers caught 1-of-4 targets for just one yard in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: Malik Nabers ends with one catch in loss Monday
news.impact: Nabers suffered a shoulder injury partway through Monday night's game and briefly left to be evaluated, but he ended up coming back and finishing out the game. He only ended with one catch for a single yard, however, which burned many fantasy managers who were relying on him. Managers should keep close tabs on his health and the health of Jaxson Dart (knee) throughout this week.

news.body: Malik Washington hauled in five of his team-high 10 targets for 56 yards while also rushing twice for five yards in the Dolphins' 24-10 Week 3 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.head: Malik Washington sees seven touches in Week 3 loss to Chiefs
news.impact: Washington has made the most of steady involvement as part of an underwhelming Miami passing attack, posting over 40 receiving yards in each of the first three games. The wideout remains another risky option in a disappointing Dolphins offense to this point, with a Week 4 contest against a disruptive Minnesota Vikings defense up next.

news.body: Malik Washington secured 4-of-5 targets for 43 yards, adding four yards on one carry in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
news.head: Malik Washington grabs four passes in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Washington has now hauled in seven combined passes over the first two weeks for an average of 13.7 yards. His production to this point is likely an indicator of what to expect for the duration of the season in the Dolphins' anemic offensive attack.

news.body: Malik Washington caught three of his eight targets for 53 yards in the Dolphins' 27-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 1.
news.head: Malik Washington catches three passes in Week 1 loss
news.impact: Washington made a modest impact despite leading the team in targets, finishing third on the team in receptions in the loss. The wideout remains another high-risk pass-catching option as part of a Miami offense searching to establish their identity as the season continues, with a Week 2 contest against the San Francisco 49ers up next.

news.body: Malik Washington caught three of four targets for six yards and a touchdown while also running twice for 22 yards in the Dolphins’ 38-10 loss to New England on Sunday.
news.head: Malik Washington scores touchdown in loss
news.impact: Washington failed to get much going as the de facto top target in the Miami offense. He’s did at least score a touchdown, but six yards on three receptions leaves a lot to be desired. He’s a depth option in deep dynasty leagues at best at this point, having failed to take advantage of his opportunities in 2025.

news.body: Marvin Harrison Jr. caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Cardinals 36-30 loss against the 49ers on Sunday.
news.head: Marvin Harrison Jr. totals 40 yards Sunday
news.impact: The talk around the NFL the past two weeks has been Harrison not being targeted by Jacoby Brissett. He was a little more involved this week, but still not enough to be trustworthy in fantasy lineups.

news.body: Marvin Harrison Jr. failed to catch his only target in the Cardinals' 31-7 loss to Seattle on Sunday.
news.head: Marvin Harrison Jr. sees one target in loss
news.impact: This is a big development for Harrison. He only caught one pass in the season opener, and now that has escalated to just a single target in this game. It's unclear if the team has given up on him, or if it's more of a lack of effort on his part, QB Jacoby Brissett looking elsewhere when targeting receivers, or some combination of all three. Either way, the team needs to figure out a way to use their 2024 first-round investment. That, or trade him away to a new team and acquire assets while he gets a fresh start.

news.body: Marvin Harrison Jr. caught only 1-of-3 targets for 33 yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.head: Marvin Harrison Jr. finishes with one grab in season opener
news.impact: Aside from one big play, Harrison did not make much of a mark for the Cardinals in Sunday's win. Quarterback Jacoby Brissett looked Harrison's way just three times, which was good for only fifth on the team. After finishing well behind fellow wide receivers Kendrick Bourne (8) and Michael Wilson (7) in targets, Harrison might be best viewed as a wait-and-see bench stash for now.

news.body: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Marvin Harrison Jr. was dealing with cramps.
news.head: Marvin Harrison Jr. dealing with cramps
news.impact: Harrison had to stop practicing a couple times on Sunday. It is a positive sign it isn't a leg or hamstring injury he is dealing with.

news.body: Matthew Golden caught 5 of 12 targets for 100 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday.
news.head: Matthew Golden snags touchdown in loss to Falcons
news.impact: Golden had several passes intended for him tipped by defensive backs after being undethrown, and another target where the DB committed a pass interference penalty. So, the five catches on 12 targets may not seem great; there is still context to be had. He is startable each week for the Packers.

news.body: Matthew Golden hauled in four of his six targets for a team-high 58 yards in the Packers' 20-17 Week 2 win over the New York Jets.
news.head: Matthew Golden leads pass-catchers in Week 2 win over Jets
news.impact: Golden has been one of the few bright spots in an underperforming Packers offense to begin the season, recording four or more receptions for over 50 receiving yards in each of the first two contests. The wideout will look for another impactful performance in a favorable Week 3 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

news.body: Matthew Golden caught 6-of-12 targets for 95 yards in the Packers 39-22 loss against the Vikings.
news.head: Matthew Golden totals 95 yards Sunday
news.impact: After a lost rookie season, Golden opened this year leading Green Bay receivers in targets on Sunday. He is in the WR3/WR4 mix heading into Week 2 for fantasy managers.

news.body: Matthew Golden was back at practice at Packers training camp on Tuesday.
news.head: Matthew Golden (toe) returns to practice Tuesday
news.impact: Golden makes his way back after missing a few days of practice. He was spotted running with the Green Bay first team offense on Tuesday.

news.body: Michael Pittman Jr. caught 2-of-5 targets for 16 yards in a 30-27 win over the Bengals.
news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. quiet in Week 3 win
news.impact: Pittman was making his return from a foot injury that sidelined him in Week 2. The expectation is that Pittman would immediately eat into Roman Wilson's playing time, but Wilson turned in a 3-60-1 performance in the win. Fantasy managers may want to avoid Pittman in Week 4 against the Browns.

news.body: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) is expected to play on Sunday against the Bengals after being considered questionable with a foot injury.
news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) expected to play on Sunday against Cincy
news.impact: Pittman should give Aaron Rodgers a reliable possession receiver over the middle of the field, opening things up for the offense. Germie Bernard tried to play that role last week, but didn’t quite have the same fluidity as Pittman. He should be a decent WR3 with upside.

news.body: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals.
news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) questionable for Sunday
news.impact: Pittman missed last week's game due to a foot injury, but he is officially questionable for Week 3 and will have a chance to make his return against the Bengals this week. He was able to practice this week, but he remained limited, so he looks like a true 50-50 at this point. Pat Freiermuth will continue to see more work if the veteran misses another game.

news.body: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) limited again Thursday
news.impact: The veteran wideout was again a limited participant at practice on Thursday. He missed last week's game due to a foot issue, but he seems to be recovering well and will have a chance to play this week. We should know more about his status when the team's official game statuses get released after practice on Friday.

news.body: Michael Wilson caught 11-of-17 targets for 89 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals 36-30 loss against the 49ers on Sunday.
news.head: Michael Wilson hauls in 11 passes Sunday
news.impact: Wilson posted his biggest performance of the early season fresh off his contract extension this past offseason. He hauled in a touchdown from Jacoby Brissett in the third quarter. He profiles as a WR3 heading into next week against the Giants.

news.body: Michael Wilson caught two of seven targets for 18 yards in the Cardinals' 31-7 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
news.head: Michael Wilson sees seven targets in loss
news.impact: Wilson failed to connect with QB Jacoby Brissett in this game, and fantasy managers will be wishing for more after such a bad showing. He wil look to bounce back against the Niners next Sunday.

news.body: Michael Wilson secured 5-of-7 targets for 56 yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.head: Michael Wilson comes up with five catches in Week 1
news.impact: With his next lucrative contract extension in hand, Wilson turned in a decent performance during Sunday's win. The fourth-year receiver finished third on the team in receptions, targets, and receiving yards, maintaining a solid rapport with QB Jacoby Brissett.

news.body: Michael Wilson has agreed to a three year, $75 million deal with the Arizona Cardinals.
news.head: Michael Wilson agrees to three year, $75 million deal with Cardinals
news.impact: Wilson was about to be playing on the final year of his rookie contract, but will now see himself attached to the team for the long haul. It will be interesting to see how his role changes, if at all, under a new coaching stafff and with Marvin Harrison Jr. back in the fold.

news.body: Mike Evans (hip) has been ruled out for the remainder of the Week 3 contest between the San Francisco 49ers and Arizona Cardinals according to Nick Wagoner.
news.head: Mike Evans (hip) ruled out Sunday
news.impact: Evans battled a hip injury prior to the Week 3 contest, hauling in three of his six targets for 34 yards and one touchdown prior to exiting. Deebo Samuel and tight end George Kittle will receive even more opportunities in the wideout’s absence for head coach Kyle Shanahan.

news.body: 49ers WR Mike Evans (hip) is officially active for Week 3.
news.head: Mike Evans (hip) officially active for Week 3
news.impact: Evans was considered questionable to play after suffering a hip injury in Week 2. He as able to practice in a limited capacity Friday and appears ready to resume his normal workload against Arizona.

news.body: Mike Evans (hip) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals.
news.head: Mike Evans (hip) questionable to play Sunday
news.impact: The veteran wideout may be sidelined this week, as he is officially questionable to play due to a hip injury that he's dealing with. If he is ruled out prior to the start of the game, expect George Kittle and Deebo Samuel Sr. to have a lot of involvement against the Cardinals.

news.body: Mike Evans (hip) won't take part in San Francisco's practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Mike Evans (hip) won't practice Wednesday
news.impact: The veteran wideout is going to be sidelined at practice on Wednesday after suffering a hip injury last week. He's hoping to play through it this week, but that is uncertain at this point. Deebo Samuel Sr. will see more work if Evans has to miss a game or two while he recovers.

news.body: Nico Collins (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Indianapolis Colts.
news.head: Nico Collins (hamstring) ruled out for Sunday
news.impact: Collins has been ruled out for a second-straight week due to a hamstring injury that he's dealing with. It could cause him to miss even more time beyond this game, but we likely won't know if that's the case until sometime next week. Dalton Schultz is the primary candidate to see more work in his absence, with Xavier Hutchinson and Jaylin Noel also likely to benefit from it to some degree.

news.body: Nico Collins remained absent from practice on Thursday.
news.head: Nico Collins (hamstring) not practicing Thursday
news.impact: Collins continues to trend towards missing a second straight game due to a hamstring injury. His status will still need to be monitored on Friday to end the practice week.

news.body: Nico Collins (hamstring) was officially a non-participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Nico Collins (hamstring) officially doesn't practice Wednesday
news.impact: The star wideout was not able to practice for the Texans on Wednesday. He is still recovering from a hamstring injury that left him sidelined last week, and it's very possible that is will force him to miss another game this week. Look for Dalton Schultz and Xavier Hutchinson to continue to see more work than usual if that's the case.

news.body: Nico Collins was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
news.head: Nico Collins (hamstring) not seen practicing Wednesday
news.impact: Collins was absent last week with a hamstring injury. He remains uncertain heading into Week 3.

news.body: Parker Washington caught seven of his 12 targets for 98 yards in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
news.head: Parker Washington goes for 98 yards in Week 2
news.impact: Washington led the Jacksonville receivers in all receiving categories while nearly reaching 100 yards in a tough matchup against Denver. The veteran has been excellent through the first two games of the season, posting 12 catches for 181 yards and a touchdown. Clearly the alpha in the Jacksonville receiving room, Washington will be a low-end WR1/high-end WR2 in Week 3 against the Patriots.

news.body: Parker Washington caught five of six targets for 83 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns.
news.head: Parker Washington snags touchdown in win
news.impact: Washington answered the call of all the offseason hype with flying colors. He scored on a 30-yard bomb from Trevor Lawrence early on in the game and kept showing up to make plays afterwards. Expect Washington to continue to be a focal point in the offense, especially if Brian Thomas Jr. were to miss any time.

news.body: The Jacksonville Jaguars are "not going to stop talking" to wide receiver Parker Washington as both sides iron out a potential contract extension, says general manager James Gladstone.
news.head: Parker Washington, Jaguars remain in contract talks
news.impact: Gladstone said the team would not hesitate to carry contract discussions into the regular season as they aim to finalize a deal with their breakout wideout. Washington had 58 receptions for 847 yards and five touchdowns last season and carries an expert consensus ranking of WR29, according to FantasPros, into his fourth NFL season.

news.body: Parker Washington (undisclosed) is participating in Jacksonville's practice on Tuesday.
news.head: Parker Washington (undisclosed) participating in practice Tuesday
news.impact: Washington has been battling an undisclosed injury of some kind for a little while now, but he was back and participating at practice on Tuesday. That's a good sign that he is close to full health, especially considering that it was a joint practice with the Buccaneers. He seems to be fully on track to play in Week 1 and remains an intriguing late-round dart throw if healthy.

news.body: Pat Bryant was unable to catch his lone target in a 20-13 win over the Jaguars in Week 2. He did add a 16-yard rush in the win.
news.head: Pat Bryant held without a catch in Week 2
news.impact: Bryant was shut out just one week after leading the Broncos in receiving. Such is life as a complementary option in a Sean Payton offense. Bryant will be a boom/bust flex option in fantasy heading into Week 3 against the Rams.

news.body: Pat Bryant caught 4-of-6 targets for 42 yards in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.head: Pat Bryant leads team in receiving Monday
news.impact: Bryant was one of the few Broncos who had a respectable showing on Monday night. He looked great at the start of the game but tapered off as it went on and as Denver continued to fall further and further behind on the scoreboard. He was the best out of Denver's receivers in this bad matchup, however, so the breakout potential seems to be there for the second-year wideout this season.

news.body: Pat Bryant is off the injury report for Sunday's AFC Championship game against the Patriots.
news.head: Pat Bryant (concussion) off injury report Sunday
news.impact: Bryant closed the week with two straight full practices. He'll be a full-go heading into Sunday.

news.body: Broncos WR Pat Bryant was a limited participant on Wednesday ahead of the AFC Championship.
news.head: Pat Bryant (concussion) limited Wednesday
news.impact: Bryant caught fire early in last week’s Divisional Round, hauling in three receptions in the opening quarter before suffering a concussion. Denver hopes the rookie can clear protocol ahead of Sunday.

news.body: Puka Nacua (hip) is officially inactive for Week 3 for the Los Angeles Rams against the Denver Broncos according to Gary Klein.
news.head: Puka Nacua (hip) inactive for Week 3
news.impact: Nacua will sit out after carrying a doubtful designation into the weekend for head coach Sean McVay, pushing veteran pass-catcher Davante Adams back into a WR1 role against a tough Denver Broncos secondary Sunday night.

news.body: Puka Nacua is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
news.head: Puka Nacua (hip) listed doubtful Sunday, expected to return Week 4
news.impact: Nacua is likely to miss a second straight game. Rams head coach Sean McVay said the expectation is he'll be good to go for Week 4.

news.body: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Puka Nacua is "not making progress."
news.head: Puka Nacua (hip) not making 'great progress'
news.impact: McVay made the comment to ESPN Los Angeles. Nacua appears likely to miss a second straight game due to the injury. Davante Adams and Terrance Ferguson will both see more more opportunity if he misses another game.

news.body: Puka Nacua (hip) officially did not take part in practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Puka Nacua (hip) officially doesn't practice Wednesday
news.impact: As expected, Nacua was not able to practice for the Rams on Wednesday and was officially sidelined. He remains uncertain for Week 3, but it sounds like the team is looking to err on the side of caution if it comes down to the wire, which would again lead to more work for Davante Adams and Terrance Ferguson (ankle) on Sunday night.

news.body: Quentin Johnston caught three of his six targets for 40 yards in the Chargers' 24-16 Week 3 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Quentin Johnston sees six targets in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Johnston has struggled to capitalize on a generous target share early in the season, recording three receptions or less on 17 total targets in the first three contests. The wideout remains one of many risky pass-catching options in an underperforming Chargers offense early on, with a Week 4 contest against the Seattle Seahawks up next.

news.body: Quentin Johnston caught 1-of-5 targets for just seven yards and rushed the ball one time for seven yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.head: Quentin Johnston struggles in loss Sunday
news.impact: Los Angeles' offense as a while struggled on Sunday, and Johnston was no exception to that. He wasn't able to haul in all but one of his five targets against the Raiders, and he only ended up contributing 14 total yards over the course of the game. He isn't worth rostering in most league formats at this point in the season.

news.body: Quentin Johnston came up with only 2-of-6 targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
news.head: Quentin Johnston does little in Week 1 loss
